articles.title: Palmeirense é empurrado, bate a cabeça e morre após suposta importunação sexual contra funcionária de hotel em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, homem estava embriagado e teria, ainda, tentado queimar um segurança com cigarro. Caso aconteceu na noite de sábado (21), após jogo contra o Flamengo.
articles.summary: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, homem estava embriagado e teria, ainda, tentado queimar um segurança com cigarro. Caso aconteceu na noite de sábado (21), após jogo contra o Flamengo.
articles.body:
Um torcedor do Palmeiras morreu na noite de sábado (21) após ser empurrado pelo segurança de um hotel na Barra Funda, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, o homem teria importunado sexualmente uma funcionária do estabelecimento antes de se envolver em uma discussão com um dos vigilantes.

Ainda de acordo com o BO, o homem estava visivelmente embriagado.

O caso aconteceu por volta das 22h40, em um estabelecimento na Avenida Marquês de São Vicente, próximo ao estádio do Palmeiras. Horas antes, o Palmeiras havia enfrentado o Flamengo pelo Campeonato Brasileiro.

De acordo com relatos de testemunhas, o homem iniciou uma confusão na parte externa do hotel e passou a discutir com um dos vigilantes. Durante o desentendimento, ele teria encostado um cigarro na orelha do segurança.

O vigilante reagiu e empurrou o torcedor, que bateu a cabeça e sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória.

O próprio segurança acionou o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu). O homem foi socorrido e levado ao Pronto-Socorro da Santa Casa, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), policiais militares foram acionados para atender à ocorrência e encontraram o homem já ferido. As pessoas envolvidas foram ouvidas, e a perícia foi acionada para analisar o local.

O caso foi registrado no 7º Distrito Policial (Lapa) como homicídio culposo, importunação sexual, injúria, lesão corporal e legítima defesa.

🔎 O registro de homicídio culposo indica que a investigação apura uma morte sem intenção de matar. A polícia também investiga a alegação de legítima defesa apresentada no contexto da intervenção do segurança.

articles.title: El Real Madrid remonta y golea a su 'víctima perfecta'
articles.standfirst: Keukelaar, con dos goles y una asistencia, lidera la victoria ante el Granada antes del parón
articles.summary: Keukelaar, con dos goles y una asistencia, lidera la victoria ante el Granada antes del parón
articles.body: El Real Madrid se ha impuesto al Granada siempre que ambos equipos se han enfrentado. La última -y séptima- ha sido este domingo en la Ciudad Deportiva nazarí, donde el conjunto dirigido por Pau Quesada ganó por 1-5 con doblete de Keukelaar y goles de Bruun, Caruso y Athenea. El partido arrancó con ritmo, pero sin grandes ocasiones. La primera de enjundia la protagonizó Keukelaar con un disparo cruzado que, tras el rechace de Laura Sánchez, no encontró rematadora en segunda instancia. Respondió el Granada con una exjugadora blanca, Iris, que tiró un caño a Jacinto para pegar un derechazo posteriormente que se fue lamiendo el larguero. Pasada la media hora de acción, el Real Madrid acosó la meta local. Primero fue Bruun la que no acertó a dar dirección a su testarazo a centro de Keukelaar; y luego Eva Navarro quien estrelló el balón en el palo aprovechando un pase entre líneas de Jacinto. Cuando mejor estaba el equipo blanco -hoy vestido de negro- llegó el gol del Granada. Iris robó un balón a Irune en línea de tres cuarto, cedió a Guridi para que ésta pusiera un centro al área y por allí apareció Gil para cabecear el cuero al fondo de las mallas. El equipo visitante pidió falta en el origen de la jugada, pero tras consultar con el FVS la trencilla validó el tanto y gol subió al marcador. El Real Madrid no bajó los brazos y logró darle la vuelta al choque en los últimos seis minutos antes del descanso. Keukelaar puso el empate de vaselina, aprovechando un nuevo pase en largo de Jacinto y ganando en carrera a su marca, en el último minuto del tiempo reglamentario; Bruun hizo el segundo cabeceando un centro de la neerlandesa en el tiempo de añadido. Las visitantes ampliaron distancias nada más comenzar el segundo acto. Apenas transcurrieron 22 segundos cuando Keukelaar remató un centro de Caicedo para anotar el tercero de su equipo. Sólo tres minutos después llegaría el cuarto, obra de Caruso, que resolvió con la zurda una nueva asistencia de Jacinto. A pesar de los goles encajados, Laura Sánchez fue la mejor de las suyas. Sacó goles que bien podían haberse cantado a Cristóbal, Caicedo y Bruun. Pasada la hora de juego, los dos técnicos agitaron el avispero buscando cambiar el sino del choque. Una de esas permutas, Athenea, sanó su ausencia en la convocatoria de la selección con un gol de disparo cruzado. Fue el punto y final para el partido más cómodo del Real Madrid este curso.

articles.title: Aberdeen: Mario Frick delivers on 'heavy metal football' promise at Kilmarnock
articles.summary: Mario Frick aimed for "heavy metal football" after taking over from Aberdeen and travelling fans were served up quite the concert at Rugby Park.
articles.body:
If "heavy metal football" is what Aberdeen did, indeed, serve up at Kilmarnock on Saturday, Dons supporters will be eager to see more of this type of concert.

New head coach Mario Frick used the phrase in the build-up to his first game in charge and his team did not disappoint.

The 4-2 Rugby Park victory was bombastic, chaotic and end-to-end - just one of six goal-laden Scottish Premiership games on Saturday.

The four Aberdeen strikes - two from Kevin Nisbet and one each from Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall - showed Aberdeen's attackers at their best with fine finishing.

In the work in progress column, though, is defending, with the visitors lapsing badly for Killie goals scored by Greg Kiltie and Tyreece John-Jules.

All in all, it was an ideal start for former Luzern boss Frick.

Aberdeen's Frick starts with win in six-goal thriller at Kilmarnock

Frick was not a complete unknown to Scottish football when he was appointed during the international break - but the reference point was somewhat obscure.

Playing for Liechtenstein at Hampden in 2010, Frick gave the visitors a shock second-half lead.

The end of that game was reminiscent of the kind of heavy metal the head coach was talking about pre-match as Stephen McManus headed Scotland's winner after Kenny Miller's leveller.

Speaking after his Premiership bow, the former Luzern boss described himself as "very happy, very proud" of his new team.

"With only three training session, you can see so many attacking patterns in that first half, which was amazing," he told BBC Scotland.

"We struggled the first few minutes with some players that hadn't played in a long long time and the 1-0 lead helped. First half was very good, the second half, complicated, because Kilmarnock played very well. We were very lucky, but at the end, I think it is a deserved victory and we are very happy."

When asked if he was happy with the players trying to show his style, Frick replied: "Yes, for sure, after two training sessions, I saw a lot of it in the first half.

"It is a good start for us, but it is just the beginning."

Former Scotland midfielder Derek Ferguson took in the match at Rugby Park and was impressed with the visitors.

"As an attacking force, I thought they were good to watch," the former Rangers player said.

"They've got a big game on Tuesday night, against Rangers, so Rangers will need to be at their best, on their toes if they're going to get a result.

"It was the perfect result, obviously, for the manager coming in.

"There was more energy, more legs, more running power. They were winning a lot of the duels.

"It's something to build on, but they've got to work on that defence. They've got to be more solid if they're going to go forward."

Next up Ibrox and a season's third meeting with Rangers.

The two previous encounters, in the Premiership and League Cup semi-final, finished 1-0 to the Ibrox side, with the winning goal coming in the second half both times.

Meetings of Aberdeen and Rangers are typically just as fraught as the Rugby Park game on Saturday.

So, more heavy metal? It probably won't be smooth jazz.

We asked for your views following Aberdeen's 4-2 win over Kilmarnock.

Allan: One simple question. Why was [Ante] Palaversa nowhere to be seen under Stephen Robinson? I think the fans are due an explanation as to why both he and [Nicky] Devlin fell so far down the pecking order.

Brian: Much, much better is probably an understatement. Great entertainment and a big threat going forward and,as long as we score one more (at least) than the opposition then I will be happy. It is very noticeable that Jack Milne is much more steady when Nicky Devlin is playing. I am looking forward to the rest of this campaign.

Mike: Green shoots of recovery evident. Working as a unit from back to front has been a rarity at Aberdeen. If this is only after three training sessions, I am drooling at the mouth for what's to come. Stiff test on Tuesday, but the confidence must be there so nothing to fear.

Fred: Very positive start under the new manager. Good to see some direct attacking play but still a problem defending. An acid test coming against Rangers.

articles.title: Man City Women 1-3 Tottenham Women: WSL champions lose again as winning home record crumbles with Spurs defeat
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Man City suffer back-to-back WSL defeats with a loss against Tottenham; Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw had put the hosts ahead; Cathinka Tandberg, Matilda Vinberg and Jess Naz scored for Spurs; Man City's 100 per cent winning record comes to an end
articles.body:
The Swede had never lost at the Joie Stadium, winning all 16 games up until this weekend. He told Sky Sports afterwards: "This is the wake-up call that we know we need to bring everything all the time. We are a great team with great players and we will bounce back, but sometimes you need a wake-up call, then we go again."

The last team to beat Man City at home in the WSL were Chelsea in March 2025. It was the Blues who beat Man City last weekend too for their first league defeat of the season and benefitted from Sunday's shock result, maintaining their two-point lead at the top of the WSL after drawing against Liverpool on Saturday.

City have slumped to back-to-back league losses for the first time since January 2025.

It looked like it was going to be another home Man City win when Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw - who had scored four hat-tricks against Spurs in the past - fired home.

But it took until the 59th minute for Man City to have another shot on target while Spurs racked up the tally. They finally made a deserved breakthrough just before half-time as Cathinka Tandberg coolly finished after some great play from Kirsty Hanson.

The hosts finally started to up their shot count in the second half, but it was Spurs who stunned Man City with two quick goals.

Matilda Vinberg had been dispossessed by Jade Rose for the opener, but redeemed herself with a goal and assist. She sped through the middle of the two defenders, collecting Drew Spence's low pass, before finishing. She then set up an unmarked Jess Naz for the third as Spurs beat Man City in the WSL for the first time since 2021.

Tottenham do remain in fifth after Man Utd's late win at Birmingham , but will surely be the last thing on their minds after a huge win. Jeglertz has plenty to ponder now over the international break to keep the title race from slipping away.1

11: GOAL! Shaw scores early Man City opener, finishing a Rose pass.

34: PENALTY?! Spurs shout for it after Carlotta Wamser's foul on Kirsty Hanson, but nothing is given by the referee.

40: GOAL! Tandberg deservedly levels for Spurs, finishing Hanson's low cross after a great run in behind.

59: SHOT! Man City have their first shot on target since scoring as Lauren Hemp's shot is pushed away by Kop.

75: GOAL! Vinberg picks up a brilliant low pass from Spence, beating her defenders before finding the net.

79: GOAL! Spurs stun Man City with a third, Vinberg setting up an unmarked Naz.

Bright questions who is leading among Man City players

Millie Bright on Sky Sports : "Man City need to tidy up without the likes of Alex Greenwood, who's a natural leader in the back line. That's where they'd looked a bit disjointed since she's been out with injury.

"It's something they need to tighten up on because some of those goals could have been prevented just with organisation, communication and everyone executing their role.

"You might take some results as a wake-up call but you shouldn't need a wake-up call when you're a team that's competing to be back-to-back champions. That's enough motivation to be on it.

"The one thing that has been lacking for me is the character - it's finding a way to win, it's the body language when something doesn't go right or you concede. Who is getting everyone together? And it goes back to that leadership without their captain at the minute."

Jeglertz: We could have had more energy throughout

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz to Sky Sports : "I'm disappointed. Tottenham are a good team and they played through us a couple times too easily, especially in the first half. Second half, we are more there but they also had some transition moments when they scored.

"It's tough but that's how it is. This league, if you're not on your top (game), the teams might punish you and they did that against us today.

"We missed a little bit of the urgency in the second half. We were one goal down and we were trying, but we lacked a little bit of the last energy and power. That was probably the thing that I felt during the second half that we could have put a bit more energy to all facets of the game.

"It's a tight league and we have done a good season so far. We have two defeats and one draw and that's OK. Of course we want to win more games, but that's how the title is today, it's going to be tough until the end. We are second in the league and battling about winning the title, but we need to do better games than this."

Ho: Winning was going to take our highest performance - and it did

Spurs boss Martin Ho to Sky Sports : "Man City are one of the best teams in world football, but I knew when we're on song, defended the way we did, pressed the way we did, we were aggressive, then we can get a result.

"It was going to take our highest performance and it did.

"The response [to the first goal] was really good. It's the way we play and it's a little bit of decision-making with the ball.

"There's going to be mistakes with the way we play, but the response is important because you grow in mentality when that happens.

"We grew in mentality when we got the goal back through Cathinka and when we started to push. Our mentality was good but we need to build on it now.

"You want to keep momentum building but the players have put in a big shift with this last three to four weeks, it's been a lot of games.

"Now they're going away on internationals for a couple of weeks and I wish them well, but you want to keep going, but I also know they need a rest."

articles.title: Burnley 2-2 Blackburn: Todd Cantwell penalty earns draw as Rovers players send message to Tony Mowbray
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Championship match between Burnley and Blackburn Rovers at Turf Moor on Sunday; Burnley took the lead on two occasions but Blackburn battled back to draw; Rovers players sent a message to Tony Mowbray, in what would have been his 900th game
articles.body:
In a gripping, physical east Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani's rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel's steered finish after the break.

But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn's first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Sky Bet Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back.

Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message 'We're with you, Tony' on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray's absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a t-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley's lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker's leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

articles.title: El Oviedo tampoco despega con Raúl y cosecha una nueva y abultada derrota
articles.standfirst: El Córdoba ganó con goles de Budesca, Diego Bri y Kevin Medina (penalti) y sigue enchufadísimo: 14 de los últimos 18 puntos
articles.summary: El Córdoba ganó con goles de Budesca, Diego Bri y Kevin Medina (penalti) y sigue enchufadísimo: 14 de los últimos 18 puntos
articles.body: El Córdoba logró una convincente victoria ante un Oviedo sin capacidad de reacción, ni al marcador en contra ni a la llegada de Raúl González tras la destitución de Calero. Budesca, Diego Bri (golazo) y Kevin Medina (penalti) sellaron los tantos califales. Ya son seis jornadas sin perder y 14 de los últimos 18 puntos de un equipo que supera a su rival en la clasificación y se acerca a zona de playoffs. El partido arrancó con mucho ritmo. Rubén Alves, en un cabezazo hacia atrás en un córner, y Diego Bri, en otro a centro de El Jebari que repelió Aarón Escandell, generaron las primeras ocasiones de los locales, mientras que el propio Alves, en un mal despeje de cabeza, casi anota para el Oviedo. En esas, una gran subida de Budesca, con remate raso, significó el 1-0 en el minuto 13. El cuadro ovetense, al que se veía incómodo, pudo igualar en un contragolpe con tiro fuera de Estanis Pedrola, aunque cerca de la media hora Samu Rodríguez tuvo que sacar en la línea un remate de Eder García que se colaba. En la segunda parte, el juego fue de arranque más trabado y con interrupciones, una fase de la que lo sacó Diego Bri con un soberano golazo de zurda, con un disparo que tocó en el larguero y entró en la red. Raúl buscó cambios, pero no generó problemas a un Córdoba que fue refrescando también el equipo y tuvo un par de opciones con Víctor Sánchez. El público abroncó a Jacobo González en su regreso y, ya en el 90', Kevin Medina transformó un penalti que él mismo forzó. Gran victoria blanquiverde para seguir escalando ante un Oviedo decepcionante.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Race Odds to Watch and Predictions for 2026 Award
articles.summary: The Heisman Trophy is Jeremiah Smith's award to lose despite the Ohio State Buckeyes' continued struggles.
articles.body:
The Heisman Trophy is Jeremiah Smith's award to lose despite the Ohio State Buckeyes' continued struggles.

Smith is a heavier favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook to win the Heisman than he was a week ago.

The Ohio State wide receiver put up another 100-yard, two-score performance in Saturday's loss to the Nebraska Cornhuskers. He personally didn't do anything to harm his Heisman resume.

A handful of quarterbacks on likely College Football Playoff teams are making a late push to challenge Smith for first-place votes, but for now, it seems like the award belongs to Smith.

Jeremiah Smith (-450; bet $450 to win $100)

Devon Dampier (+600; bet $100 to win $600)

Jeremiah Smith recorded his seventh 100-yard receiving yard game, and third in a row, in Saturday's loss to Nebraska.

Smith also scored two more touchdowns to give him five multi-score games on the season.

He leads the FBS in receiving yards (1,482) and touchdown catches (17) and ranks third in receptions (86).

Smith consistently put up eye-popping numbers despite Ohio State's poor performances as a team.

There's no question Smith is the best player in college football, and as long as he puts up decent numbers against the Michigan Wolverines next week, he should collect a large amount of first-place votes.

The best player on one of the best teams in college football typically ends up with the Heisman.

Devon Dampier is trying to make a late case for himself in the discussion alongside Smith as the quarterback of the only undefeated team in the FBS.

Dampier threw for 278 yards and ran for 62 more yards in the Utah Utes' win over the TCU Horned Frogs.

The Utes scored 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Dampier threw and ran for a touchdown during the late surge.

Dampier has two games left to sway voters in his direction. He should put up strong numbers against the West Virginia Mountaineers on Friday and then he'll get a chance to beat a top-15 team in the Big 12 Championship Game.

Darian Mensah had an off for someone in need of putting up big numbers to challenge Smith for the Heisman.

The Miami Hurricanes quarterback threw for 241 yards in a win over the Virginia Tech Hokies, but he was picked off twice, completed 67.6 percent of his passes and didn't record a touchdown pass.

Mensah hadn't thrown more than one interception in a single game this season before Saturday.

The season-long numbers of 29 touchdowns, four interceptions and 3,317 passing yards are still very impressive for Mensah.

He deserves a nod as one of the Heisman finalists, but in order to grab first-place votes, he needs to go off against the Boston College Eagles next week and then in the ACC Championship Game versus the Wake Forest Demon Deacons.

Gio Lopez at least deserves a mention in the Heisman discussion.

He's thrown for 2,701 yards and 21 touchdowns inside one of the FBS' most explosive offenses.

Lopez has led the Wake Forest Demon Deacons to 99 points over the last two weeks.

Wake Forest put up 268 points over its last five games to confirm its spot in the ACC Championship Game.

Lopez has the numbers of a Heisman finalist, but he might not receive enough votes to challenge Smith or Dampier for a top spot in the final results.

That could change, though, if Lopez leads Wake to an ACC title with a win over Mensah and Miami in two weeks.

articles.title: Cignetti Reacts to Indiana's Loss to Unranked Washington After Controversial Remarks on CFP Rankings
articles.summary: After calling out the College Football Playoff rankings earlier this month, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti is now singing a different tune following Saturday's upset loss to unranked Washington.
articles.body:
After calling out the College Football Playoff rankings earlier this month, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti is now singing a different tune following Saturday's upset loss to unranked Washington.

Cignetti and the defending national champion Hoosiers were served a dose of humble pie, as their hopes for a second straight title took a major hit when the Huskies tipped Paddy McAteer's 37-yard field goal attempt wide in overtime to steal a 27-24 victory.

"I give Washington a lot of credit; great win for them," Cignetti said after the loss, per the Associated Press . "Our guys fought in the second half, but they made one more play than we did, and that was it."

It was just 10 days ago that Cignetti trolled the CFP selection committee for dropping Indiana from No. 4 to No. 9 in its second batch of rankings:

It now seems like Cignetti's bravado has dissipated, as the Hoosiers would've been one win away from their second straight trip to the Big Ten championship game had they beaten the Huskies. Now, the team will need to beat Purdue in next week's regular-season finale and get some extra help from around the conference. Missing the conference championship game would diminish Indiana's chances of qualifying for the 12-team College Football Playoff.

Cignetti still appears to be searching for answers after making some interesting personnel decisions on Saturday. He substituted Josh Hoover back in for starting quarterback Grant Wilson in the third quarter after Wilson nearly threw an interception.

"I went in fully hoping and believing Grant would do well and make it through the whole game," Cignetti said. "We just got a little shaky there, something I sensed. Josh came in and made a few plays."

A blocked field goal in the third quarter also led Cignetti to sub kicker Nico Radicic for McAteer, but that move proved ineffective as well.

"We've missed too many field goals this year," Cignetti said. "The other guy had made them. That was the plan going in; we gave him an opportunity, and he missed the field goal."

articles.title: Remontada de campeón del Barça
articles.standfirst: El Barcelona mantiene la ventaja en el liderato después de superar un 0-2 al Villarreal en una gran segunda parte. Lamine, que falló un penalti, decisivo en los dos goles finales
articles.summary: El Barcelona mantiene la ventaja en el liderato después de superar un 0-2 al Villarreal en una gran segunda parte. Lamine, que falló un penalti, decisivo en los dos goles finales
articles.body: Remontada de campeón del Barça para mantener la ventaja sobre el Real Madrid en el liderato de LaLiga. Los de Flick fueron sorprendidos por un gran Villarreal en una primera parte que acabó con 0-2 con los goles de Buchanan y Oluwaseyi, pero los azulgranas le dieron la vuelta en una segunda parte para enmarcar dirigidos por un excelso Lamine Yamal. Los goles de Gerard Martín, Fermín y Pau Navarro en propia puerta valieron tres puntos importantes para un equipo que mostró dos caras, la de salir dormido en algún partido y la del equipo goleador cuando se pone la pilas. Esta vez funcionó la segunda. Las bajas condicionaron una jornada más la defensa del Barça. Flick optó por poner a De Jong de central junto a Gerard Martín con Eric García y Cancelo en los laterales. Desde el saque de centro se vio que el Villarreal iba a hacer una fuerte presión buscando que el Barça tuviera posesiones cómodas. Y no le pudo salir la mejor la jugada, la presión amarilla provocó un error de pase de Fermín que acabó en los pies de Buchanan, que se sacó un zapatazo desde fuera del área para batir a Joan García. Era el minuto 5. Y dos después un robo de Buchanan sobre De Jong propició una contra con pase en largo de Moleiro sobre Oluwaseyi para que este batiera a Joan García con un fuerte remate por alto. El doble mazazo surtió efecto en un Barcelona al que se vio ansioso, sobre todo un Fermín que no se quitaba de la cabeza su fallo en el 0-1, y que buscaba cuanto antes recortar distancias, pero la contras amarillas merecían mucha atención en defensa. A los 21 minutos tuvieron los de Flick una gran oportunidad para recortar distancias tras una ingenuidad de Oluwaseyi dejando el pie atrás ante una internada de Lamine en un penalti claro que no vio en un principio Alejandro Hernández, pero un aviso posterior desde la sala VOR le hizo rectificar. Lo tiró Lamine, que le pidió el balón a Raphinha, pero lo falló después de que el fuerte viento que hacía en Barcelona impidiera que lo lanzara con normalidad en un par de ocasiones. Quedaba claro que Iñigo Pérez tenía bien estudiado al Barcelona. Con el Rayo se lo hizo pasar muy mal a los de Flick y con el Villarreal consiguió que apenas le crearan peligro hasta el descanso. Al margen del penalti, un remate sin convicción de Adeyemi y una jugada embarullada en el área tras una internada de Eric García fueron las únicas ocasiones en que Gulácsi tuvo que intervenir. El Villarreal defendía con orden su ventaja, pero quedaba una larga segunda parte para intentar que los tres puntos se fuera para la provincia de Castellón. El inicio de la segunda parte fue el esperado. Un acoso y derribo sobre la portería de Gulácsi que provocó que Pau Navarro y Freeman vieran tarjeta amarilla en los primeros minutos. Un primer aviso flojo de Pedri fue seguido de un tiro cruzado de Fermín y después de otro de Cancelo que obligaron a Gulácsi a enviar ambos a córner. De este último saque de esquina protestado por el Villarreal llegó un centro de Pedri que cabeceó Gerard Martín a la red. En el minuto 57 se metía el Barça en el partido y con mucho tiempo por delante para intentar la remontada. Los de Flick no cedieron en su empeño y cinco minutos después Fermín enmendó su error en el 0-1 para marcar el 2-2 con un remate ajustado al poste a pase de Lamine Yamal. El 10 azulgrana quería más y sólo cuatro minutos después una nueva internada suya por banda acabó con un fuerte centro hacia Eric García que introdujo en su propia puerta Pau Navarro. Remontada en 20 minutos de un equipo campeón para no perder el liderato. Salieron Dani Olmo y Gordon y el inglés fue una nueva pesadilla para la ya superada zaga amarilla. El Villarreal tiró la toalla tras el 3-2 y ni con los cambios ofensivos de Iñigo se vio un atisbo de recuperación. Estaba más cerca el 4-2 que el 3-3 sobre todo en un gran disparo de Dani Olmo que despejó Gulácsi con una gran intervención. Con los nervios habituales al estar el partido abierto se llegó al final del partido con la victoria de un Barça que cuando se pone las pilas es intratable. El líder mantiene su ventaja.

articles.title: Carlos Espí, el ángel de la guarda de Mourinho: "Me da pena que no le den más minutos"
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Real Madrid se ha convertido en una de las piezas clave del técnico luso
articles.summary: El delantero del Real Madrid se ha convertido en una de las piezas clave del técnico luso
articles.body: Carlos Espí se está convirtiendo en una de las grandes sensaciones del Real Madrid. Su nombre vuelve a estar en boca de todos después de decidir el encuentro ante el Celta con un gol en el minuto 85, apenas seis minutos después de saltar al terreno de juego. Una nueva aparición desde el banquillo que ha desatado los elogios y ha abierto un debate: ¿merece el delantero más protagonismo? Sus cifras hablan por sí solas: cuatro goles en 93 minutos. Casi nada. En 'Marcador', Fernando Sanz puso el foco en el rendimiento del equipo blanco, que no firmó precisamente su mejor actuación, pero encontró motivos para el optimismo. "Partido flojo del Real Madrid, partido de los que vimos a principio de temporada y que nos desesperaba, pero muy positivo en la entrada de Vinicius y, sobre todo, en la entrada de Espí", reconoció. El exfutbolista fue todavía más contundente al valorar el papel del delantero: "Es un jugador que, después de lo de hoy, se merece muchos más minutos de los que está disputando. Yo creo que es un jugador que podría hacer muchísimos goles en el Real Madrid, que de hecho los va a hacer". Sanz también destacó una de las características que más está conquistando al madridismo: su compromiso. "Esa lucha, ese sacrificio, ese punto de honor, ese juego en equipo, esa humildad, yo creo que son las características de un jugador del Real Madrid", explicó. Uno de los elogios más significativos llegó desde dentro del vestuario. Thibaut Courtois quiso poner en valor las características de Espí y, especialmente, aquello que aporta al juego ofensivo del equipo. "Tiene presencia, es un tío alto, fuerte y que sabe dónde tiene que estar. Es un delantero nato", explicó el guardameta belga. Courtois también estableció una comparación con otros perfiles de la plantilla, como Mbappé, para explicar por qué la presencia del joven delantero resulta tan importante. "Al final, Kylian y otros son jugadores menos de área, un poco más de estar al borde; no siempre les gusta estar ahí. Cuando entra Carlos tiene esa presencia y nosotros podemos estar más alrededor y entrar", señaló. El portero recordó incluso cómo se desarrolló la jugada del gol ante el Celta: "Cuando entró, llegó un gran centro de Vini, un gran remate, una parada y el rebote menos mal que fue para nosotros. Un buen gol y estoy muy contento por él". Además, reconoció que no resulta sencillo encontrar minutos cuando Mbappé ocupa la posición de delantero centro: "Kylian es el nueve y no hay muchos minutos para él. Pero la verdad es que cuando entra los aprovecha y eso es importante". El entrenador portugués explicó que Espí tiene unas características muy concretas, propias de un delantero de área, y que su aportación no depende necesariamente de acumular muchos minutos. "Carlos es un jugador de área, no tan asociativo. Es un chico que tiene una calidad en el área, que ataca bien el primer palo, el segundo palo, que juega de espaldas... La historia del fútbol está llena de jugadores decisivos como él jugando poco", señaló. El técnico también destacó su actitud y su relación con el grupo: "Es un tipo de chico que no se embarca en historias de que tiene que jugar más, es un chico feliz de estar en el Madrid y que tiene el respeto de su entrenador, de sus compañeros y de su afición". El luso, eso sí, dejó abierta la puerta a darle más oportunidades desde el inicio: "Espero poder darle partidos desde el inicio o la titularidad". Mientras los elogios se multiplican, Espí mantiene los pies en el suelo. El delantero reconoció que marcar en el Santiago Bernabéu tiene un significado especial. "Yo creo que es el más especial. Se me han dado muchos días en meter aquí, en el Bernabéu, con todos los madridistas, y la verdad que es un día que no voy a olvidar", confesó. Su fórmula para aprovechar las oportunidades es sencilla: trabajo y preparación. "Estar preparado, trabajar cada día para estar preparado, como he dicho, para no tocarme del míster, sean cinco, sean diez, sean treinta", explicó. También reconoció que, como cualquier futbolista, desea tener más minutos, aunque aseguró estar muy contento con la confianza recibida de Mourinho. La celebración reflejó el cariño que se ha ganado dentro del vestuario. "Somos toda una familia. Se ha visto en la celebración. La verdad es que estaba agachado porque me estaban dando por todos lados", bromeó. Incluso tuvo tiempo para vivir otro momento especial al encontrarse con Rafa Nadal, presente en el Bernabéu: "Una leyenda como Rafa Nadal, que esté ahí presente, hablando conmigo, ha sido muy bonito". El debate sobre su protagonismo también llegó de la mano de Javier Tintó, que puso sobre la mesa unos datos especialmente llamativos para reivindicar al delantero. "Espí es que ha jugado solo 65 minutos y lleva un gol menos que Bellingham, cuatro más que Vinicius, más que Endrick, los mismos que Diomandé. Me da pena que no le den más minutos", afirmó. Una reflexión que vuelve a poner el foco en la eficacia del atacante. Su capacidad para aparecer en momentos decisivos, incluso con oportunidades muy limitadas, está convirtiéndole en un recurso cada vez más valioso para Mourinho. Ante el Espanyol, frente al Elche y ahora contra el Celta, Espí ha vuelto a demostrar que puede ser decisivo cuando el equipo más lo necesita. Fernando Sanz, Mourinho, Courtois y Javier Tintó coinciden en destacar sus virtudes. Su siguiente reto es transformar esos minutos de oro en una oportunidad mayor. De momento, el Bernabéu ya tiene un nuevo nombre al que corear.

articles.title: Revisen el vídeo, es urgente
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Barcelona-Villarreal
articles.body: A principio de temporada, Hansi Flick decidió de manera unilateral que Raphinha era el capitán del equipo. Se vivía un momento de confusión porque Ter Stegen se había ido al Ajax, Araujo al Liverpool y Frenkie de Jong estaba lesionado y no podía jugar. Existía un evidente vacío de poder que solucionó el técnico. La verdad es que la decisión no sorprendió a nadie porque todos conocían ya el rol del brasileño dentro del vestuario, a pesar de no llevar el brazalete. A lo largo de esta temporada, Raphinha ha confirmado con creces que es, con justicia, el capitán del equipo. Pero hay jugadas que definen lo que es Raphinha para este equipo. La prueba se dio frente al Villarreal. Pedri perdió un balón en la medular, seguramente el único que perdió en todo el encuentro, y el Villarreal lanzó una contra vertiginosa. El brasileño se pegó un sprint a toda velocidad para ayudar en defensa, porque era un tres contra uno. Pues superó a todos sus contrincantes y recuperó el balón cerca del córner. Pero la cosa no acabó aquí: Raphinha salió lanzado para iniciar desde ahí la contra de su equipo. Dos paredes perfectas y balón a Lamine para que asistiera a Fermín en el segundo gol. Revisen el vídeo, busquen la jugada y que todos tomen ejemplo. ¡Chapeau! Lamine lo buscó él solito. Un doble regate del azulgrana acabó en penalti, si bien Hernández Hernández tardó una barbaridad en concederlo y no lo hizo hasta que revisó la jugada en el VAR. Pero, al igual que le había pasado a Mbappé el día anterior, lanzó el balón fuera. Ya se veía que algo así podía pasar porque, debido al fuerte viento, el balón no se quedaba quieto en el punto de penalti. Tercer penalti fallado por Lamine de los siete lanzados en Liga. Igual habría que darle las gracias a Luis de la Fuente porque le dio muy pocos minutos en los dos partidos que la selección jugó en el pasado parón. Pedri realizó este domingo posiblemente el mejor partido de la temporada. Seguramente estaba más fresco que el resto, pero el canario fue siempre la referencia de su equipo, el director de orquesta que necesitaba una remontada después del 0-2. Fue un auténtico espectáculo ver cómo buscaba espacios y se iba de los rivales. Y asistió a Gerard en el primero. No hay que descartar la opción de Frenkie de Jong como central. Es verdad que no le gusta jugar ahí, que siempre reivindica su rol como centrocampista, pero, viendo lo que hizo frente al Villarreal, ha quedado claro que es un recurso perfectamente válido para cuando sea menester. Estuvo muy bien a nivel defensivo, solidario en el esfuerzo y, sobre todo, sacando perfectamente el balón desde atrás, convirtiéndose en una perfecta ayuda para los centrocampistas. Fermín tiene su carácter. Para lo bueno y para lo malo. De entrada, perdió un balón a los cinco minutos que significó el primer gol del Villarreal. Le puede pasar a cualquiera. A partir de ahí, se puso las pilas para enmendar el error. Lo buscó sin descanso y no paró hasta que consiguió el segundo gol. Pero iba tan revolucionado que, después de ser sustituido, vio la roja y fue expulsado.

articles.title: FSU Targets Georgia DC Schumann, Latest Rumors on HC Search After Mike Norvell's Firing
articles.summary: Florida State reportedly has zeroed in on its next head coach target after firing Mike Norvell earlier this month.
articles.body:
Florida State reportedly has zeroed in on its next head coach target after firing Mike Norvell earlier this month.

According to ESPN's Pete Thamel , the Seminoles' coaching search "is focused on" Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. Thamel added that there is "mutual interest," and discussions are "expected to pick up in the near future."

Schumann started his coaching career in 2008 as a student assistant at Alabama under legendary coach Nick Saban. He followed Kirby Smart to Georgia when Smart was hired as head coach in 2016, and he was elevated to co-defensive coordinator in 2019 before assuming the full-time role in 2024. He helped lead the Bulldogs to back-to-back national championships in 2021 and 2022.

This season, Schumann has presided over a unit that ranks sixth in the nation with averages of 267.0 yards allowed and 13.9 points allowed per game. Georgia improved to 10-1 with Saturday's 34-6 win over South Carolina, with the Bulldogs holding highly touted quarterback LaNorris Sellers to just 87 yards and an interception on 10-of-18 passing.

Norvell was fired on Nov. 1 after the Seminoles fell to 3-5 with a loss to Clemson. He ended his nearly seven-year tenure at Florida State with a 41-39 record, including 23-30 in ACC play. He led the team to back-to-back bowl game appearances in 2022 and 2023, his only winning seasons with the program.

Florida State fell to 5-6 with Saturday's 28-10 loss to NC State. The Seminoles will close out the regular season on Black Friday against in-state rival Florida before turning their attention back to Schumann and their coaching search.

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Con este árbitro siempre nos pasa lo mismo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Barcelona analiza el triunfo de su equipo ante el Villarreal y el arbitraje
articles.summary: El técnico del Barcelona analiza el triunfo de su equipo ante el Villarreal y el arbitraje
articles.body: Hansi Flick compareció ante los medios para analizar el triunfo de su equipo frente al Villarreal. Una victoria complicada porque el conjunto azulgrana se vio con un 0-2 en los primeros diez minutos de partido. El alemán estaba molesto por el arbitraje y las tarjetas que vieron sus jugadores y él mismo. "Estoy muy contento por el triunfo después de que ellos se pusieran por delante con un primer gol por un claro error nuestro. Ya en la primera parte tuvimos ocasiones para marcar y en la segunda mitad ya jugamos mucho mejor y estuvimos bien estructurados. Creo que merecimos el triunfo". "No sé por qué expulsaron a Fermín. De hecho se lo pregunté a ellos y por eso vi la amarilla. Lo que sí sé es que el cuarto árbitro estuvo todo el partido mirando a nuestro banquillo. Yo intento ayudar a los colegiados en el campo. No sé qué pasó ni qué le dijo. Necesito más información"". "Estoy contento con los árbitros, pero con este siempre nos pasa lo mismo. Es lo de siempre. Y si esto va a ser así sólo nos queda jugar mejor para ganar. Como hicimos en la segunda parte. "Cuando te fijas en los primeros diez minutos podemos decir que no empezamos nada bien. Sabíamos que era un equipo que venía a presionarnos. Nos costó y encajamos dos goles. La reacción de equipo fue increíble, incluso en la primera mitad. Tuvimos ocasiones como el penalti. En la segunda parte teníamos una estructura clara de juego y jugando así el rival se cansa, es normal. Logramos marcar tres goles en 10 minutos. Increíbles". "Si el resultado hubiese sido otro no diría nada. Pero, en el caso de hoy, lo que hemos visto era algo previsible. Estoy muy contento con el arbitraje en general, pero con este árbitro, no. Todos siempre se fijaban en nosotros, nos miraban a nosotros. Se puede hacer de forma diferente: hablar, explicar... pero no nos dicen nada. Cómo lo puedo decir... creo que la mayoría de árbitros te hablan, explican...Pero si las cosas suceden como hoy, hay que jugar mejor. Con este hambre de volver, remontar, marcar.... hemos jugado contra un rival de Champions y la primera mitad han defendido muy bien dentro del área. Todo el mundo está contento por los seguidores y tres puntos más". "Este partido de hoy ha sido uno de los mejores. Cómo ha controlado, hemos, el centro del campo, los momentos de los partidos, los tempos, velocidad de juego... en el caso de De Jong y Gerard en el eje de la defensa han hecho un trabajo fantástico. Para Frenkie no es fácil esa posición. Si te fijas en el resultados puedes decir que dos chutes a portería y dos goles. Pero creo que hemos merecido la victoria". "No lo sé. Creo que siempre es lo mismo. Me lo puedo imaginar que la gente lo vea de esa manera pero esta temporada me gustaría ser más calmado. Hoy tengo que apoyar a mi equipo y aportar la energía desde la banda y, si sucede algo fuera, puedo no estar de acuerdo. Por eso me han enseñado amarilla. Se trata todo de comunicación. No sé, la verdad". "Lamine también ha marcado unos cuantos. Se ha decidido sobre el terreno de juego. Hablará con ellos y veremos cómo lo gestionamos en el futuro. Los dos pueden marcar desde el punto de penalti". "Rodri es un jugador increíble, pero el resto de centrocampistas también lo están haciendo muy bien. Fermín después de su error, ha mejorado mucho. No es fácil cuando estás perdiendo de dos goles". "Es una opción, por supuesto. Es increíble cómo ha jugado con el balón. Si tienes que estar en esa última línea no es fácil, es más cómodo hacerlo desde la medular porque siempre que tienes alguien detrás. Su actitud en esa demarcación nos ayuda y eso nos ha demostrado, sobre todo, con el balón. Hablábamos si poner Eric de central y De Jong de lateral... y creo que tomamos la decisión acertada". "No he hablado con él y tampoco hablo con los agentes. Los necesitamos a todos. Tenemos 8 partidos antes del siguiente parón y los necesitamos a todos. Eric y Cancelo han jugado increíble. No es fácil para él disputar de minutos, pero lo importante es que esté a un buen nivel mental aunque es cierto que si no juegas, no puedes ser el más feliz".

articles.title: Florida State reportedly looking at Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann to replace Mike Norvell
articles.summary: Schumann has worked with Kirby Smart for the entirety of his coaching career.
articles.body:
Has Florida State identified its next head coach?

According to ESPN , the Seminoles are "focused" on current Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. The 36-year-old has been Georgia's sole defensive coordinator since the 2024 season after operating as the team's co-defensive coordinator for the previous five seasons.

Florida State is looking for a new head coach after firing Mike Norvell following a loss to Clemson earlier this season. The school owes Norvell roughly $50 million thanks to a contract extension he signed after the Seminoles went undefeated during the 2023 regular season.

In Norvell's 32 games after the 2023 season, FSU went 10-22.

Schumann has worked with Georgia coach Kirby Smart for the entirety of his coaching career. After starting out as a student and then graduate assistant at Alabama when Smart was an assistant under Nick Saban, Schumann came to Georgia as the Bulldogs' inside linebackers coach when Smart was hired at his alma mater in 2016. After Mel Tucker left to be Colorado's head coach following the 2018 season, Schumann and current Oregon coach Dan Lanning became Georgia's co-defensive coordinators.

After beating South Carolina 34-6 on Saturday night, the No. 1 Bulldogs are allowing fewer than 14 points per game this season. Georgia has given up fewer than 10 points in three of their past four games, and its four wins since a home loss to Auburn have all been over teams ranked in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings at the time.

Florida State's search for Norvell's successor couldn't proceed in earnest until an athletic director was found. The school recently hired Jeff Purinton to lead the athletic department after Michael Alford was fired in September.

The Seminoles fell to 5-6 on Saturday with a loss to NC State. It was the school's first loss in three games under interim coach Rick Stockstill, and the defeat means FSU needs to beat Florida in Week 13 to make a bowl game.

articles.title: Desire Doue injury: PSG forward to have surgery on ruptured ACL
articles.summary: Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.
articles.body:
Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night .

Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.

The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.

The European champions have been plagued with injury issues so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.

PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino made mistakes in Man Utd’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool but the size of the mess he has inherited is clear
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of Manchester United turned into an Anfield nightmare as his side were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool. Adam Bate was there to see it unravel as Pochettino was confronted with the reality of the mess that is United...
articles.body:
Dismal defending, confused combinations, conceding in clusters, confidence long departed. And that all evident in the first quarter of an hour of what was never a contest. This is the only team in the Premier League without a win since August for a reason.

Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino. The new boss might be only days into a contract that runs until 2029, but it has not taken him long to see the mess he has inherited. Liverpool had this match won in 13 minutes. Unlucky for Pochettino.

And yet, even at this early stage of his reign, the Argentine cannot escape blame entirely. The decision to give Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in almost a year was exposed as an error immediately. He was partially culpable for Leny Yoro's red card.

De Ligt's inability to judge the flight of the ball and then appear to give up the chase entirely was not the sort of support his young centre-back needed. Whatever the verdict on the decisions of Yoro and the referee, the Dutchman was given the runaround.

His only previous start in any competition this season came in Como, where United were dismantled, and it all looked too quick for him. One wonders what Pochettino saw in training. Thrusting him into a game of this intensity was a massive mistake, regardless.

Maybe the subsequent substitutions will raise a few eyebrows too. The only way back into the game was on the counter-attack but the removal of Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha robbed United of any pace on the breakaway. That was a strange call too.

Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans paired together in midfield? That one might already have been discredited. And somehow the struggling De Ligt, desperately short of match fitness, was asked to labour on for the full 90 minutes of what was a chastening defeat.

The change of role for Diogo Dalot was a smarter switch - and an easy win for the coach - given how the Portuguese player had been caught out repeatedly in that left-back position under Michael Carrick. But the truth is that there were no real positives here.

The bar was so low as well. The seven previous away days had yielded no wins but a number of horrible moments. From the humiliation at Hull to the late equaliser conceded at Everton. From the crushing in Como to Carrick's final away defeat to Chelsea.

But in its own way, this was just as devastating to morale.

The dice have been rolled with this appointment, fragile hopes raised. When the fans in the Kop were mockingly chanting 'Poch is at the wheel' with 15 minutes still to go, and the fourth Liverpool goal yet to go in, it was a clue that the day had unravelled spectacularly.

Pochettino is not getting 'sacked in the morning' as the Kop repeatedly suggested, but the nature of this defeat means that his immediate challenge is to rebuild shattered confidence. What Ralf Rangnick once famously called open-heart surgery must wait.

How do you press high with defenders who do not feel comfortable following? How do you keep a compact midfield in the gap that this creates when mobility is a major weakness? Issues for another day. Ones that will take work and windows to fix, not mere weeks.

And yet, Pochettino will have to think short term as well as long. The Premier League table demands that on the day Hull City went six points clear of them. United are only one from safety, but can there be any confidence of them easing away from danger?

Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino.

articles.title: Hull City 2-0 Brighton: Oli McBurnie's late double stuns Seagulls after Konstantinos Tzolakis' goalkeeping heroics
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Oli McBurnie's late double earns Hull a shock 2-0 Premier League victory over dominant Brighton following Costinha red card; Tigers goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis produces string of fine saves to deny visitors before added-time goals
articles.body:
Like the legendary Greek mythological king, Tzolakis had the Midas touch throughout for the Tigers, making five first-half saves - the most by any goalkeeper all season - before McBurnie netted twice in added time to snatch a victory that had looked beyond Hull for so long.

High-flying Brighton had racked up an xG of 2.24 and five presentable chances but were denied by a combination of the goalkeeper's fine form and some wasteful finishing, and ultimately missed the chance to move three points off leaders Arsenal.

Tzolakis' highlight was a stunning one-handed stop to keep out Diego Gomez's 15th-minute effort, which set the tone for a perfect performance to frustrate the visitors.

He was also at his best to deny Georginio Rutter, after Yasin Ayari's shot had rebounded off the crossbar, before a superb stop with his trailing leg frustrated Gomez again moments before the interval.

"We can be critical of some of the misses but the goalkeeper has been fantastic," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane at the break. "He's man of the match already for me."

With the one-way traffic unabated after the restart, Tzolakis owed some credit to midfielder Regan Slater for keeping his clean sheet intact, nodding off the line when substitute Charalampos Kostoulas lifted the ball over the goalkeeper after he had given the ball away cheaply himself.

The hosts did threaten with Mohamed Belloumi twice cutting in off the right before wasting good positions, and Sorba Thomas almost netting a fortuitous goal when his cross bounced back off the crossbar.

But, after Brighton's Costinha was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge late on, Hull saw their moment to strike, with McBurnie scrambling in an opener following a counter-attack before tapping home a second with the Seagulls pushing to equalise.

Having been dropped by Greece during the international break following a 7-0 hammering by Netherlands, Tzolakis provided the perfect response with an unstoppable performance between the sticks.

The 24-year-old has been a hit on Humberside since his summer move from Olympiakos but was at his very best to earn them a first home win since August.

It was his second entry into the top 10 of xG prevented in individual matches this season, the only goalkeeper to manage such a feat.

Statistically, he performed better across 90 minutes in Hull's 1-0 win away at Coventry early in the campaign - another where their opponents had dominated - but his individual saves against the high-flying Seagulls were even more impressive.

They lifted him into fifth place in the season rankings of over-performing goalkeepers, ahead of Premier League greats Alisson and David Raya.

Though the Greek stopper would never claim to be on their level - yet - Hull increasingly look like they have a gem on their hands nonetheless.

Match-winners credit each other for victory!

Hull City's double goalscorer Oli McBurnie to Sky Sports:

"He [Tzolakis] was unbelievable, the cat today. He has been all season for us to be fair to him. We give him a bit of stick about his gear and that, but he's been good in net.

"He was fantastic, kept us in the game and that's how we want to play. We know if we are always in games we fancy ourselves to get chances and make it as horrible as possible and that's what we did."

Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to Sky Sports:

"So many saves but two goals from Oli. It was a team effort and everyone helped each other.

"We are a unit here like a team. We play for each other. We saw a very good team effort, and we deserved to take the three points.

"In the first half we suffered a lot but we managed the second half and scored in transition two goals from Oli and that's it."

15: ONCE... Tzolakis begins his afternoon heroics by getting down low to keep out Gomez's effort.

19: MISS! Costinha should put Brighton ahead but fires wide from close range.

37: TWICE... Ayari's effort crashes off the bar before Rutter is again denied by Tzolakis on the follow-up.

45+3: THREE TIMES A 'KEEPER! Tzolakis keeps out another Gomez effort thanks to a superb stop with his trailing leg.

52: CLOSE! Gomez brings down a cross with a world-class first touch before lashing inches wide of the far post.

65: CLOSE! Against the run of play, Belloumi fires wide after leaving Olivier Boscagli on his backside.

79: OFF THE LINE! Kostoulas races through to latch onto Slater's backpass but the midfielder recovers to clear his chip off the line.

89: RED CARD! Costinha sees red for a clumsy lunge on Thomas, which earns him a second yellow card.

90+1: GOAL! McBurnie turns home an unlikely opener on the counter-attack to stun Brighton before...

90+4: GOAL! ...He adds a second from Belloumi's square ball to seal victory and send the MKM Stadium wild.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Spurs 'a match for anyone' as win at Man City boosts European dreams
articles.summary: Women's Champions League qualification may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham at the start of the season - but they are firmly in the mix after winning at Manchester City.
articles.body:
Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.

The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.

But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.

Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.

They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.

"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.

"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL

Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.

They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.

Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.

The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.

What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.

Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.

Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.

Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.

That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 – until Tottenham tore up the script.

The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.

Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.

After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.

After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.

Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.

"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.

"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."

Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.

In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.

They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.

"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.

When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.

Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.

Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.

It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.

Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.

There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

articles.title: Dundee Utd: Zidane Iqbal loving life at Tannadice after World Cup
articles.summary: Zidane Iqbal is starting to live up to his famous name and wowing Scottish Premiership fans after his move to Dundee United.
articles.body:
Given the superlatives being thrown in the direction of Zidane Iqbal by the Scottish football fraternity, one would think he was a replica of a certain France great instead of just sharing his name.

So much so that BBC Radio Scotland pundits were suggesting on Saturday's Sportsound that the 23-year-old is the answer to Celtic's hunt for a long-term successor to captain Callum McGregor as their midfield general.

It is just as well for Dundee United that the Iraq international is tied to them until at least the summer, his early season appearances for Utrecht ruling out a transfer during the January window.

So, where has he sprung from and what is all the fuss about?

Hibs 0-4 Dundee United: What Goodwin said

Midfielder inspiring United 'masterclass'

Born in Manchester to a Pakistani father and an Iraqi mother, Iqbal came through the Old Trafford youth system.

He signed his first professional contract with United in 2021 and became the first British-born South Asian and first-ever British South Asian to play in the Champions League when he came on as an 89th-minute substitute against Young Boys that December.

However, that was to be his one and only first-team appearance and, although he had already made his international debut in a World Cup qualifier at the age of 19, he was sold to Utrecht for a reported fee of £1m in summer 2023.

Starting off in their Jong Utrecht second string, he would go on to make 49 appearances for the Dutch top-flight outfit before making a surprise switch to the Scottish Premiership this summer.

On the one hand, United were getting a player who played all three of Iraq's games at this summer's World Cup, two of them starts, albeit all three were heavy defeats.

On the other hand, Iqbal had only managed seven appearances last season for Utrecht and had been a second-half substitute in two of their four matches at the start of the new campaign.

However, after a pivotal display in what was being described as a midfield "masterclass" by United in Saturday's 4-0 dismantling of hosts Hibernian , manager Jim Goodwin revealed he always had belief the Tangerines were unearthing a "Rolls-Royce".

"The head of recruitment's job is to go and identify good talent for us," Goodwin told BBC Scotland. "It's my job to give him the profile and then he goes out and does the groundwork.

"We could see immediately when we watched the footage of Zidane and when we had the Zoom call with him and his representatives, we not only had a fantastic player but a really good person with the right characteristics to come and fit the culture here."

While on-loan Rangers man Lyall Cameron was among the goals and fellow 24-year-old Dylan Tait provided a stylish assist, it was the third leg of what some regard as the best midfield triumvirate in the Premiership who was singled out for most praise at Easter Road.

With former Celtic winger Aidan McGeady again pondering the question about McGregor's likely successor, transfer market expert and former United wing-back Allan Preston opined: "A six for Celtic? Look no further than young Iqbal.

"He's been magnificent since he's come to Scottish football, absolutely brilliant. Running the show again.

"If Celtic are looking for a young boy at his age with experience, he is a full international, knows the game, played in Scotland, you can see what he can do, there's your man in front of you.

"Other players' hair's on fire, but he's just nice and calm. He's at a different level. He doesn't panic. When the ball comes to him, he is so calm on it, he takes his time, he's got great peripheral vision."

The former Dundee United wing-back pointed out, though: "He's had his two clubs that he can play for in a year of football, so he is going nowhere until at least the summer, so enjoy him while you can because I think you'll get serious money for this young boy."

McGeady pointed to Iqbal's "good pedigree", having started with Manchester United and already having 32 caps for Iraq, but wondered if that would be enough for Celtic to consider him.

"I don't even think, if he's performing this well, Celtic will go and get him," said McGeady.

"Why are Celtic not looking at players like this? Do they feel they have to prove themselves somewhere else first?"

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown was similarly impressed.

"He's been a delight to watch - sharpness to get on the ball and willingness to drive forward," the former midfielder and manager pointed out.

"He beats a man in the middle of the park as well and there's not too many midfielders willing to do that.

"Watching him there talking to the media, he can't get the smile off his face. He enjoys football, he takes the ball under pressure, he does things that other people don't do, especially in midfield.

"He brings composure, but he can also drive through as well. His willingness to keep getting on the ball, even if he makes that slight mistake - that's what I really enjoy watching about him."

Drive from Netherlands to Scotland 'worth it'

While Goodwin reckons there will be likely interest in the summer, Iqbal has no thoughts of so quickly leaving a club - and manager - who have resurrected his club career.

"I'm not even looking at any other clubs," he told BBC Scotland. "I'm fully focused on Dundee United.

"They've given me a platform to enjoy myself and play football. I'm really enjoying my football again.

"They've given me faith and confidence. The gaffer and the coaching staff have a lot of belief in me.

"The bare minimum I can do is pay them back with strong performances and hopefully it carries on."

Iqbal recalled being at Manchester United's "development centre since I was four or five - I signed when I was eight", explaining that he "then left for some first-team football".

He stressed that his lack of games last season came as a result of "a couple of injuries" and, while "I learnt a lot in Holland", he is "happy to have left that behind me", adding: "That book's closed now."

Visit our Dundee United page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Get Dundee United news notifications in the BBC Sport app

Iqbal also recalled how Goodwin's enthusiasm persuaded him to make the switch to Tannadice on deadline day.

"After the World Cup, I had one year left on my contract and I was in touch with my agent," the midfielder said. "We both wanted a move and I had a few chats with a few clubs.

"To be fair, I left it a bit late for Dundee United, but after the first call with the gaffer, I straight away called my agent after we ended the call.

"I said, 'look, I genuinely feel like the guy really believes in me'.

"It happened very late. I had to drive from Holland to Scotland. It was a tough drive but worth it in the end."

That World Cup was also a defining experience, with representing his country in the United States described as surreal.

"Having your friends and family there to watch you and playing on the world stage, with so many people, was a dream," he said.

"Playing against top players gave me that confidence boost I needed. I thought I did well in the three tough games.

"I knew, wherever I'd end up, with the faith of the gaffer, I could really kick on and push because I've learnt so much from the World Cup."

Goodwin is the manager to have done that and Iqbal added: "He's such a top guy, not just in football.

"His tactics are amazing. Everyone's comfortable. Everyone wants to fight for him."

articles.title: Dylan Raiola's NFL Draft 2027 Stock Updated by Top Expert After QB's Impressive Stats with Oregon
articles.summary: Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola has been very good this season in relief of Dante Moore, throwing for 1,929 yards, 16 touchdowns and two interceptions while leading the team on its current four-game winning streak.
articles.body:
Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola has been very good this season in relief of Dante Moore, throwing for 1,929 yards, 16 touchdowns and two interceptions while leading the team on its current four-game winning streak.

But is that enough to garner him some legitimate attention ahead of the 2027 NFL draft?

According to Dane Brugler of The Athletic, "Raiola would have to do something pretty special in the Playoff to consider going pro. Credit to him for getting better with each start as he gets more comfortable with the offense and develops chemistry, but the volatility in his game remains a key concern in his NFL projection. He is a loose passer, which is both a positive and negative, but his lack of mobility will be a concern against NFL speed. If Raiola is looking to maximize his development, he will stay in college for another year."

Oregon Finds Stride With 3rd Straight Win 🔥

While a CFP appearance once felt like a pipe dream after a 4-3 start this season, the unranked Ducks have wins over Ohio State, Northwestern and Michigan and Michigan State since and still have a real chance of sneaking into the Big Ten title game (though they still need to beat Washington). And if they do get in and Raiola leads them on a deep run, NFL teams would find that impossible to ignore.

articles.title: Women's Scottish Cup: Celtic, Rangers, Glasgow City, Hearts & Aberdeen progress with big wins
articles.summary: Holders Celtic as well as Rangers, Glasgow City, Hearts, Montrose, Aberdeen and Falkirk progress with big wins in the Women's Scottish Cup.
articles.body:
Holders Celtic breezed through to the fourth round of the Women's Scottish Cup with a 17-0 victory over Forfar Farmington .

Morgan Cross and Casey Howe both netted hat-tricks, Isabella Fisher scored four times and Amy Gallacher bagged a double.

Lauren Doran-Barr, Addie Handley, Maria McAneny and Evie Rabjohn also scored and Forfar conceded an own goal.

Last season's beaten finalists, Rangers , were 5-0 victors at home to Motherwell .

Mijke Roelfsema opened the scoring with her first Rangers goal, Eilidh Austin made it two and Laura Berry converted a penalty shortly before going off injured.

Fallon Connolly-Jackson got her maiden Rangers goal early in the second half and Hannah Blake completed the scoring.

Glasgow City defeated Cambusdoon 10-0. Leah Lane scored her first City goal, with Kelly Brady, Lisa Forrest, Abi Harrison, Yuuka Kurosaki, Jesi Rossman and Emily Whelan also on target.

Sofia Maatta netted twice and Cambusdoon conceded an own goal.

Reigning Scottish champions Heart of Midlothian won 6-0 away to Stenhousemuir .

Lucy Jane Hope put the visitors in front and Jenny Smith doubled their lead. Ava Crawford got the third, Monica Forsyth also netted and Hope and Forsyth added to the tally.

Montrose won 13-0 at Dunipace , with Neve Guthrie, Kaela McDonald-Nguah and Hannah Stewart each scoring once, Francesca Ogilvie netting twice, Darcie Miller bagging a hat-trick and Demi Taylor picking up a four-goal haul, with an own goal also aiding the visitors.

Spartans were 11-2 winners at home to Bonnyrigg Rose . Zara Andrews and Ronaigh Douglas both scored once, there were doubles for Emily Cadell, Tegan Reynolds and Izzy Young, while Emma McMurdo scored a hat-trick.

Mya Christie, Holly Daniel, Christie again and Briana Salvetti all netted in Aberdeen's 4-0 home win over Dryburgh Athletic .

SWPL2 side Boroughmuir Thistle won 2-1 on penalties against top-flight Partick Thistle after a 1-1 draw. Imogen Longcake gave the visitors a second-half lead, but Amy Denholm levelled to force extra time.

Falkirk were 7-0 winners at home to Renfrew . Maisy Stewart, Skye Neillie, Mhari Smith, Caitlin McFarlane and Olivia Murphy all scored first-half goals, with McFarlane and Emma Lawson adding to the rout after the break.

Queen's Park beat Dundee United 2-1, with Ellie Kane and Darcy Molloy putting the hosts two up at the break and Lucy Stevenson replying in the second half.

Rossvale won 3-2 at home to Gartcairn . Maddie Wilson and Sarah Petherick had Rossvale 2-0 up, but Clare Docherty replied for the visitors before the break. Petherick's second proved to be the winner, with Gartcairn's Madison Maxwell netting a late consolation.

Livingston v Hamilton Academical was abandoned at half-time with Hamilton a goal up, while Inverurie Loco Works v Bishopton, Kilmarnock v Hibernian and Westdyke v St Johnstone were postponed.

articles.title: Asturias, patria de Las Palmas
articles.standfirst: Hace tres semanas ganó al Oviedo y hoy hace lo mismo ante el Sporting para dar un golpe de autoridad
articles.summary: Hace tres semanas ganó al Oviedo y hoy hace lo mismo ante el Sporting para dar un golpe de autoridad
articles.body: Las Palmas, patria querida. Asturias de mis amores... Y es que el equipo de Albert Sánchez sumó su segunda victoria a domicilio en el Principado de Asturias tras hacerlo en su debut –en el banquillo grancanario– en el Carlos Tartiere y repetir triunfo ayer en El Molinón-Quini. El conjunto insular fue mejor que el Sporting y lo hizo patente por medio de dos buenos goles, ambos con asistencias de Iván Jaime. El inicio prometedor del Sporting lo cortó rápido Las Palmas con una propuesta atrevida. Los pupilos de Albert Sánchez manejaban las posesiones, mientras que los rojiblancos buscaban golpear con la más clara para Jorge Sáenz después de un error defensivo de los amarillos. No ajustició el central local, lo hizo pagar Las Palmas. A través del balón parado, Manu Fuster encendió la llama, Iván Jaime activó la mecha y Enzo Loiodice puso la guinda para rematar una preciosa jugada a balón parado: saque de córner. Hacía justicia Las Palmas, por lo visto sobre el terreno de juego gijonés, a una versión rácana del Sporting en su casa y antes sus aficionados. Nada cambió tras el paso por vestuarios. Las Palmas manejaba el ritmo del partido ante un Sporting incapaz de generar algo peligro. El equipo grancanario aguantaba sin problemas y atacaba bien a la espalda. Ahí llegó el segundo tanto, tras una gran contra que Iván Jaime regaló a Miyashiro. Sin margen de reacción rojiblanca, Las Palmas tuvo, incluso, el tercero en el tiempo añadido.
