articles.title: Zabiri firma el triunfo del Racing
articles.standfirst: El marroquí marcó los dos goles con los que el conjunto cántabro se puso 0-2 y provocó el penalti para el 3-2, tras el empate de una Real que mereció más
articles.summary: El marroquí marcó los dos goles con los que el conjunto cántabro se puso 0-2 y provocó el penalti para el 3-2, tras el empate de una Real que mereció más
articles.body: El Racing de Santander enlazó por primera vez dos triunfos seguidos en esta LaLiga y sigue fuerte en El Sardinero, al ganar a la Real Sociedad en un espectacular partido que pudo tener muchos más goles y que decidió la sensación Zabiri, con doblete y el penalti que provocó para el tercero El partido prometía y no defraudó desde el inicio. Canales tuvo la primera ocasión clara, con un remate cruzado desde el punto de penalti que se le fue desviado por poco, contestando la Real con un zurdazo cercano de Sergio Gómez que repelió Agirrezabala y otro de Oyarzabal que no fue gol porque Belocian sacó el balón sobre la misma línea. Sí que terminó en el fondo de la red la primera aparición de Zabiri, que chutó un muy buen pase de Iker Luque. La diana debió de dejar muy ‘tocado’ a Remiro, que poco después no regateó bien al marroquí en su presión y vio como el pichichi del Racing ponía el 2-0 a los ocho minutos de juego. Canales chutó al palo, pero en jugada que no valía. Agirrezabala se lució para evitar que Sergio Gómez acortara distancias. Sarr cabeceó fuera de inmediato. Guedes lo hizo flojo a las manos del portero local. Óskarsson tampoco acertó La Real dominaba, pero Zabiri buscó el hat trick en su tercera y cuarta apariciones. Agirrezabala rechazó el zurdazo de Sucic. Fort evitó providencial el 0-3 de Zabiri que tampoco logró con un testarazo Pablo Ramón. Antes del descanso, Oyarzabal logró en semifallo el esperanzador 1-2 para los txuriurdin, con un palo de Canales antes de la retirada. El Racing volvió a salir a tope, con cuatro llegadas con peligro en ese mismo número de minutos, despertando con un centrochut de Fort fuera por poco una Real que continuó con su asedio al conjunto cántabro y encontró el premio con el empate a dos que Guedes logró con un derechazo de los suyos que tuvo la colaboración de esta vez un mal Agirrezabala. Cuando parecía que los txuriurdin tenían el partido controlado, Zabiri, ¡vaya pesadilla! provocó un penalti de Remiro que Canales convirtió. Guedes casi empató en la siguiente jugada y Óskarsson falló una de esas que no se pueden fallar, salvando Sergio Gómez la sentencia de Iñigo. El portugués, en dos ocasiones, y Oyarzabal, hasta en cuatro, tuvieron la igualada, pero el Racing se quedó con un triunfo firmado por Zabiri, la gran sensación de lo que llevamos de LaLiga.

articles.title: What's still at stake in every conference title race ahead of the final week of the 2026 college football regular season
articles.summary: Indiana could find itself on the wrong side of Big Ten tiebreakers after losing to Washington.
articles.body:
Hardly any conference title game participants have been decided ahead of the last week of the regular season.

We know both participants in just two of the 10 conference championship games after Week 12. And in conferences like the Big Ten, there are more than three teams who enter Week 13 with a legitimate chance to win a conference title.

Here's how each conference race stands after Saturday's games:

UTSA or Memphis or East Carolina or North Texas

The Roadrunners are a game ahead of the other three teams following a road win at UAB on Saturday night. North Texas lost at Tulane on Saturday afternoon, while Memphis lost to Navy and East Carolina beat Army.

To make things simple, UTSA is in with a win over Tulsa in Week 13. Memphis plays Temple, East Carolina plays FAU and North Texas plays UAB. The Mean Green didn't play either Memphis or ECU, while Memphis has the head-to-head win over the Pirates. If there's a three- or four-way tie, the highest team(s) in the CFP rankings will be chosen for the title game.

This one is easy. The Hurricanes beat Virginia Tech to clinch a spot in the title game and Wake Forest beat Georgia Tech. Miami won the regular-season matchup between the teams 33-20 and Wake Forest has the head-to-head tiebreaker for second place over Louisville.

The Utes can finish no lower than second in the Big 12 regular-season standings after a win over TCU on Saturday night. The final spot in the title game comes down to the Red Raiders and Cougars. If both win or BYU loses, Texas Tech is Utah's opponent. If Tech loses to TCU and BYU beats Cincinnati, BYU will get a rematch with Utah thanks to Tech's loss to the Bearcats earlier in the season.

The Bruins are a game ahead of the other three after a loss to Michigan and are in the Big Ten title game with a win over USC. If UCLA loses and everyone else wins, Oregon and Iowa would win the four-way tiebreaker and meet in Indianapolis.

A three-way tie at 7-2 for second place also goes against Indiana. The Hoosiers lost to Washington on Saturday, Iowa has already beaten the Huskies and Oregon has Washington in Week 13. The Hoosiers play Purdue, while Iowa plays Nebraska on Black Friday. The Huskers beat Ohio State on Saturday.

The top two teams in Conference USA didn't meet in the regular season. Liberty is 10-1, but likely out of the College Football Playoff picture thanks to one of the weakest schedules in the country.

Toledo or Western Michigan or Buffalo or Ohio or Miami (OH)

The first four teams listed above are tied at 6-1 in conference play while the RedHawks are 5-2. They need a lot of help. But they also get Western Michigan in Week 13.

Ohio plays Toledo, too. And Buffalo gets two-win Akron. The Bulls have to be considered the favorite to make the title game.

New Mexico or North Dakota State or Wyoming or Air Force or UNLV

The Lobos have one loss while every other team has two. New Mexico hosts Air Force in Week 13. A win means UNM will host the MWC title game.

Both NDSU and Wyoming are 6-2 and done with conference play. UNLV, which beat New Mexico but lost to both Air Force and Wyoming, has Nevada in Week 13.

Boise State vs. San Diego State or Texas State

The Aztecs threw a potential wrench into Boise State's College Football Playoff plans with their comeback win late Saturday night. SDSU has the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas State thanks to a 31-29 win earlier in the season, too. Texas State plays at Utah State in Week 13, while San Diego State goes to Washington State. If both win, SDSU heads to Boise State.

Georgia vs. Alabama or Texas or Tennessee

The Bulldogs clinched a spot in the title game with a win over South Carolina on Saturday night. The other three teams are 6-2 in the SEC. According to the SEC Network, here are the clinching scenarios for Texas, Alabama and Tennessee.

Texas: win and Alabama loss; or win and Tennessee loss; or win and Alabama win and Tennessee win and loss by either Mississippi State or LSU

Alabama: win and Tennessee loss and Texas loss; or win and Tennessee win and Texas win and Mississippi State win and LSU win

Louisiana Tech vs. Georgia Southern or James Madison

The Bulldogs won the West division with a 7-0 conference record so far. Georgia Southern is a game ahead of James Madison in the East, but JMU won the head-to-head matchup. If GSU beats Louisiana Tech — yes, they could meet two weeks in a row — they're in the conference title game. If Louisiana Tech wins and JMU beats Coastal Carolina, the Dukes will meet the Bulldogs.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Red-Card Controversy Called Out by Rival Coach as Video Goes Viral from Miami's Loss
articles.summary: Columbus Crew head coach Laurent Courtois believes Lionel Messi should have received a red card after hitting Gonzalo Tapia in the head with a throw-in during Saturday's 3-0 win over Inter Miami.
articles.body:
Columbus Crew head coach Laurent Courtois believes Lionel Messi should have received a red card after hitting Gonzalo Tapia in the head with a throw-in during Saturday's 3-0 win over Inter Miami.

"Everyone knows that was more than a yellow card," he told reporters, adding the situation was "sad."

Both Messi and Tapia were instead given yellows.

"It's a play in the match. I don't know if it's a red card, but I am not the referee to say," Tapia told reporters. "It stays there."

It was a massive decision nonetheless. Had Messi been given a red card he would have missed the team's next match, a do-or-die contest for Inter Miami as they look to stay alive in the MLS playoffs.

Columbus leads the best-of-three first-round series 1-0, with Messi's men needing to beat them twice in a row to keep their season alive.

articles.title: Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Mauricio Pochettino endures nightmare start as Leny Yoro's early red card sparks collapse
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Manchester United are routed by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino's first game; Leny Yoro received early red card before Liverpool ran riot; defeat keeps Man Utd in relegation zone, one point off bottom
articles.body:
Yoro saw red in the eighth minute when he was adjudged to have made a last-man foul on Alexander Isak, with Dominik Szoboszlai slamming home the resulting free-kick.

The decision was contentious, with Isak having seemingly lost control of the ball when he was fouled, but the double blow left the visitors in disarray and Florian Wirtz added an acrobatic second only two minutes and 46 seconds after the opener.

Liverpool fans taunted Pochettino with chants of 'you're getting sacked in the morning' following the second goal.

The Argentine's decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt a first Premier League start in 357 days backfired spectacularly, with the 27-year-old misjudging a high ball in the lead-up to Yoro's red card before the hosts punished more shambolic defending after the break.

Rio Ngumoha added the third when he converted Bradley Barcola's low cross following a rapid counter-attack, becoming the youngest scorer in the history of the fixture, with substitute Victor Munoz netting the fourth from a through ball by the excellent Wirtz.

The four-goal loss showed Pochettino the size of the task ahead and keeps United in the Premier League relegation zone, only a point off the bottom. They have conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's major leagues in all competitions, with 34.

The scoreline could easily have been worse for them, with Barcola and Isak among those to miss chances as Liverpool racked up 28 shots, 10 of which came from Wirtz passes.

The defeat was the heaviest in a Manchester United manager's first game since Lal Hilditch was beaten by the same scoreline a century ago, in 1926. It is the first time in 40 years that United have been in the bottom two at this stage of a season.

For Pochettino's counterpart Andoni Iraola, the result represents his first statement win since taking charge. Liverpool move back into fourth place, only a point behind Manchester City in third and seven points behind leaders Arsenal.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino to Sky Sports :

"So painful. So disappointed. It's not okay to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

"The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened.

"We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy."

Iraola: Our fans deserved this performance

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola on Sky Sports :

"I enjoyed it. I have to do a lot more but I think we wanted to celebrate in that moment. It's nice to enjoy it with the fans.

"The supporters deserved it. We've been very good away and not good enough at home. It's always a big game against Man Utd.

"They played with 10 for most of the game but we still did our job.

"We created enough to score more than four, we missed chances.

"We need to be more ruthless, but luckily today it was not needed."

Neville: Man Utd have worst defence in Europe

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville : "This is where we've got to, where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as if it's just the norm and what should be accepted.

"The club standards have dropped so far, it's incredible.

"But the fan standards haven't dropped. They expect a Manchester United team to be competitive every single week, and what they're seeing now - Manchester United have got the worst defence in the whole of Europe, and they're currently second from bottom in the Premier League.

"It's absolutely remarkable. You couldn't write it."

Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane : "United were desperate. So bad.

"Gary Neville's okay with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? Four-nil is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done!

"People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what?

"We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

"Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine. It's unbelievable chances they had.

"And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing."

Since the start of the 2021/22 season, Liverpool's four wins by four goals or more against Manchester United are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another across all competitions.

Adjusting for three points for a win, Manchester United's eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since the 1972/73 season.

That is also the previous season in which the Red Devils only managed one win through their first 11 league matches.

Mauricio Pochettino suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a Manchester United manager in his first game, along with a defeat by the same scoreline for Lal Hilditch in October 1926.

This was the quickest Liverpool had gone 2-0 up in a Premier League match against Manchester United, going two ahead after just 12 minutes and 40 seconds.

Pochettino is the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

Manchester United will end the day in 19th position in the Premier League, with this the first time since November 1986 that they have been within the bottom two places of the league table having played at least 10 matches.

Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card was the earliest shown to a Manchester United player in a Premier League match.

articles.title: Sigue el drama: paliza del Liverpool al United en el debut de Pochettino
articles.standfirst: El Manchester jugó con 10 jugadores desde el minuto 8 por roja directa a Yoro
articles.summary: El Manchester jugó con 10 jugadores desde el minuto 8 por roja directa a Yoro
articles.body: Esto ya va en serio. Y es que, señores, el Manchester United está en franco peligro de caer en esta Premier y descender a la segunda categoría. Se demostró de nuevo en otro fracaso en Liverpool, en lo que fue el debut del nuevo entrenador Mauricio Pochettino en el United. Es verdad que el conjunto de Mánchester jugó con uno menos desde el minuto 8. Pero igual: este United tiene mala pinta. Es penúltimo en la tabla de la Premier. ¡Ojo! El debut de Pochettino, por el que el United pagó 10 millones de dólares a la Federación de los Estados Unidos, no pudo empezar de forma más desgraciada. Minuto 8. Roja a Yoro en un ataque al espacio de Isak, que se iba ya hacia puerta. Roja (tercera en los últimos cuatro choques)... y gol de Dominik Szoboszlai en la consiguiente falta al borde del área. Peor imposible. Bueno, sí. Fue peor. Minuto 13', golazo de Florian Wirtz (cuarto en sus últimos cuatro partidos) tras jugadón de Rio Ngumoha. 2-0 y el United que rezaba para no recibir más goles, pues Isak falló un par de ocasiones y el meta visitante Lammens estuvo acertado (salvo en el gol de falta). Entró Maguire para compensar la roja a Yoro, se fue Mbeumo; y, tras el descanso, se fue Cunha. Estaba claro que lo que quería Pochettino era no empeorar un balance que ya es trágico: su equipo sólo ha ganado tres de los 19 partidos jugados hasta hoy en todos los torneos. Por su parte, el 'Pool' sólo ha perdido en Premier ante City y Arsenal y Fenerbahçe en Champions. Los 'reds' se quedan cuartos a siete puntos del líder, el Arsenal y a un punto del segundo y el tercero: City y Brighton. La segunda parte, obviamente, fue de dominio completo de los locales. Isak seguía fallando goles; Barcola estuvo a punto de hacer el 3-0; pero el ridículo para los de Mánchester vino con el gol de Rio Ngumoha (minuto 66') y 4-0 el del español Víctor Muñoz (minuto 82'). El campeón del mundo había salido minutos antes. En fin, 4-0, ya con nuevo entrenador en el banquillo... y pudo ser peor pues Lammens paró varias para una goleada de (mayor )escándalo.

articles.summary: How Liverpool and Manchester United's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino's reign as Manchester United manager got off to a dismal start as his side were beaten 4-0 by rivals Liverpool after playing 82 minutes with 10 men.

Here's how BBC Sport rated the players - and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Alisson Becker : Caught one cross and took a few goal-kicks. Made a good save to deny Bruno Fernandes in stoppage time. Had little else to do. 6

Ronald Araujo : Never really tested defensively. Made a few contributions going forward. 7

Jeremy Jacquet: Went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo in the box at 0-0, although a penalty against the French defender would have been harsh. 6

Virgil van Dijk: Organised the defence well. Also had a header well-saved at 0-0 and nodded another wide in the second half. 7

Milos Kerkez: Always keen to drive Liverpool up the pitch. Had some nice link-ups with Rio Ngumoha. 7

Dominik Szoboszlai: Fantastic driven free-kick to open the scoring. Went close a few more times with long shots and generally bossed the midfield. 8

Alexis Mac Allister: Did all the simple things right and allowed others to shine around him. Forced Senne Lammens into a top save in the first half. 7

Bradley Barcola: Missed a few chances to score his first league goal for Liverpool when through one-vs-one. Showed his electric pace to set up his side's third. 7

Florian Wirtz: Readjusted well to net Liverpool 's second and assisted their fourth. Five goals in four games for club and country now and looks close to his creative best. 8

Rio Ngumoha: So direct and skilful. Scored Liverpool 's third with a calm finish. Also set up their second after easily beating Diogo Dalot. Club and country have a real talent on their hands. 9

Alexander Isak: Led the line well but missed some big chances. Won the free-kick that resulted in Szoboszlai's goal and led to Leny Yoro's sending off. 6

Victor Munoz (on 72, Barcola): Good cameo and took his goal well, curling it into the far corner. 7

Trey Nyoni (on 72, Mac Allister): Looked bright. Had a shot go just over. 6

Subs not used: Chiesa, Mamardashvili, McConell, Tsimikas.

Senne Lammens: Could he have done better with the opener? Good save to deny Mac Allister and some decent stops after that. 6

Leny Yoro: Did he have to make the tackle on Isak? It was almost as though he thought about whether he should and decided the answer was yes. Given Liverpool scored from the free-kick it was a bad decision. 4

Matthijs de Ligt: First Premier League start in almost 12 months in middle of a back three turned into a nightmare with the early error that led to opening goal and Yoro red card. Struggled from that moment on . 4

Lisandro Martinez: Fully extended by Liverpool 's attack. The least bad of the visitors' starting defence, but that isn't saying much. Exposed completely by Barcola for Liverpool 's third. 5

Diogo Dalot: Given a torrid time by Ngumoha, which prompted Pochettino to bring on Maguire . Tries hard but it's not enough. 5

Youri Tielemans: Concerns about a midfield partnership with Mainoo emerge again. Not having the sustained impact required for a player of his experience. 4

Kobbie Mainoo: Twenty-one-year-old being asked to shoulder so much responsibility in an ailing team. New midfield recruits have not helped him. 5

Bryan Mbeumo: Couple of decent bursts came to nothing, then sacrificed after Yoro red card. Received consoling pat on the head from his new boss. 5

Bruno Fernandes: Early free-kick just wide and shot straight at Alisson. Given the carnage at Old Trafford this season, no wonder contract talks on hold. Furious at free-kick given against him when he thought he was through. 5

Patrick Dorgu: Asked to do an awful lot, initially as wing-back, then further back. Lucky Barcola fluffed his lines or his failure to keep an offside line would have been exposed. 5

Matheus Cunha: Tried to keep simmering frustration in check. Not easy in a losing side with no service. Replaced at the break. 5

Harry Maguire (on 22, Mbeumo): Couldn't have expected to be called on so soon. Went into middle of back three and immediately blocked an Isak effort to prevent a third goal. Tried hard. 5

Joshua Zirkzee (on 46, Cunha): Pre-match rumours of a rare start proved unfounded. Replaced Cunha at half-time and asked to bring a different skillset to the number nine role. More physical but not as good and lost possession too easily. 4

Mason Mount (on 65, Tielemans): Only on for a couple of minutes when attempted crossfield pass went to Liverpool player and eventually a third goal. 5

Noussair Mazraoui (on 65, Dorgu): Not really sure what he was supposed to do. Tried to push forward as United's poor control brought more pressure. 4

Subs not used: Heaton, Amad Diallo, Heaven, Lacey.

articles.title: Sonny Dykes Fired by TCU, Latest Contract Buyout Details & Top HC Replacements After Loss
articles.summary: TCU fired head coach Sonny Dykes on Sunday following Saturday's 38-17 loss against No. 2 Utah.
articles.body:
TCU fired head coach Sonny Dykes on Sunday following Saturday's 38-17 loss against No. 2 Utah.

The Horned Frogs are now just 5-6 on the season, which Pete Nakos of On 3 reported will continue with defensive coordinator Andy Avalos as the interim head coach.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on the buyout information and shared a statement from athletic director Mike Buddie:

One possibility to replace him is promoting Avalos, given that the defense has been largely solid this season. External options could include UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor, North Texas head coach Neal Brown and Houston offensive coordinator Slade Nagle, among others.

A recent two-game losing streak at North Texas has taken some shine off Brown's name, though he still has the Mean Green at 7-4 on the season. Nagle is guiding one of the top offenses in the sport at Houston (35.0 PPG, 18th in the nation) and would instantly instill some excitement to the program. And Traylor has UTSA at 9-2 on the season.

There's also a litany of big-name head coaches currently without gigs, including Brian Kelly, Jimbo Fisher, Hugh Freeze and Mike Norvell. And New Mexico's Jason Eck remains the hot name in the coaching carousal , with the Lobos 9-2 on the season.

TCU is going to have competition for any candidates, with Baylor also having a head-coaching vacancy.

Whatever direction TCU goes, a change became necessary.

Dykes, 57, led the team to a 13-2 record and the National Championship Game during his first season in 2022. Since then, however, the Horned Frogs have gone just 28-21 under his watch and just 17-18 in the Big 12.

TCU is a Power 4 school and has a proud tradition, but they may not be the first choice for some of the top candidates given vacancies at schools like Florida State and Baylor.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United match ends with 4-0 loss to Liverpool after early red card
articles.summary: A straight red in the 8th minute brought United down to 10 men, and gave Liverpool a chance to take an early lead on the way to the dominant shutout.
articles.body:
So far, the grass is not looking greener for Mauricio Pochettino.

On Sunday, the former United States men's national team manager had his first game as head coach of Manchester United since his sudden departure. But Pochettino's return to the Premier League did not get off to a triumphant start: Man United fell 4-0 to Liverpool, with an early red card fueling the rout.

The Red Devils were forced down to 10 men in the eighth minute, after Leny Yoro was given a straight red . The card came after Yoro caught a streaking Alexander Isak from behind, denying the Liverpool forward a clear goal-scoring opportunity.

The card gave the Reds a free kick just inside the penalty arc; Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszla took the shot direct from the kick, sending it through the wall and past goalkeeper Senne Lammens to take things from bad to worse for United.

Just minutes later, Florian Wirtz grew Liverpool's lead with a spinning volley that went up and in to the goal.

It was not an auspicious first half in the slightest, with Pochettino accidentally making a bit of history: The combination of a red card and two concessions in the opening half of the manager's debut match is a first in Premier League history, per OptaJoe .

Things didn't get much better in the second half: Liverpool grew the lead to 3-0 in the 66th minute behind a great wing-to-wing sequence, with Bradley Barcola finding 18-year-old forward Rio Ngumoha for the score.

Víctor Muñoz gave Liverpool another goal in the 82nd minute, hitting a one-two with Wirtz and a beautiful finish off a poor defensive clearance from United. That was enough to seal the 4-0 rout and start Pochettino's tenure on a very sour note.

United's best chances of the game came in stoppage time, with Bruno Fernandes getting a breakaway and Harry Maguire getting the header on the subsequent corner kick.

But other than that, the Red Devils were shockingly ineffective on offense while down a player, recording 10 shots (four on target) — compared to a whopping 28 shots (11 on target) for Liverpool. The score could have been even worse, as Lammens picked up seven saves and forced Liverpool to miss on six big chances allowed by the struggling United defense.

Taking over Manchester United was always going to be a tall challenge for Pochettino: The legendary club is starting the season in freefall, garnering only one win across the first 10 games of the season. Former manager Michael Carrick, a club legend who joined the team at the end of last season, had spent the entire start of the 2026-27 season on the hot seat.

Pochettino's name started to emerge as a coaching replacement before Carrick was even fired. But things began to move very quickly after Carrick was officially sacked , with the club reaching out to the USMNT to hire him away. Bringing Pochettino on board cost United $10 million, as part of a clause in the extension Pochettino had signed just a few months ago.

After Sunday's loss, United is currently sitting in 19th place out of 20 spots, and is in danger of relegation for the first time in the club's history if the skid continues. Including the four-goal drubbing, the Red Devils have already allowed 23 goals, second only to woeful 20th-place Crystal Palace.

articles.title: Liverpool thrash 10-man Man United in nightmare start for Pochettino
articles.summary: Leny Yoro’s red card for Manchester United after just eight minutes paved the way for a 4-0 football defeat at Anfield.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his Manchester United reign as the 10-man Red Devils were humbled 4-0 by old rivals Liverpool at Anfield Stadium.

Leny Yoro’s red card eight minutes in set the tone as Andoni Iraola’s side raced into a 2-0 lead after just 13 minutes and spurned a host of chances before adding to their advantage after the break.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions – the most of any top-flight team in any of Europe’s major leagues. But in truth, the hosts could well have matched, or even surpassed, their famous 7-0 victory in 2023 in this fixture.

Pochettino’s side sit 19th, a point off the bottom of the table, in English football’s Premier League, with eight points from 11 games. Meanwhile, the Reds are up to fourth, seven points behind leaders Arsenal.

Liverpool were already well on top when the game turned after eight minutes as Matthijs de Ligt – who struggled throughout after being handed his first Premier League start in 357 days in Pochettino’s first selection – was caught out by a long ball down the left channel which allowed Alexander Isak to race towards goal.

Yoro chased him back and, despite a heavy touch from the Swede on the edge of the box, his clumsy challenge just outside the area led to a straight red card for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

Matters got immediately worse for the visitors as Dominik Szoboszlai whipped home the low free kick, beating Bruno Fernandes on the end of the wall and the dive of Senne Lammens in goal to find the bottom corner.

It was 2-0 just three minutes later, when the lively Rio Ngumoha glided into the box on the left and fired a cross into the middle, which Florian Wirtz pirouetted to turn home with a close-range volley off the underside of the bar.

With United in disarray at the back, Pochettino brought on Harry Maguire in place of Bryan Mbeumo to form a five-man defence.

Although the visitors found a foothold in the game, the home pressure continued as Isak and Ngumoha fired narrowly past the post while Alexis Mac Allister was denied by a smart save from Lammens and Isak’s shot on the turn was somehow deflected over the top by the diving Maguire.

Szoboszlai saw a long-range effort tipped over by the flying Lammens shortly after the turnaround and saw another effort saved soon after.

Bradley Barcola spurned a glorious chance of a third just before the hour after beating the offside trap, but dragged a tame effort well wide with only Lammens to beat.

Isak missed another wonderful chance after de Ligt misjudged a bouncing ball to allow him another clear run on goal, but the Swede lashed wildly past the near post when one-on-one with Lammens.

Barcola fired over the bar after spinning away from de Ligt on 65 minutes, but the Frenchman nipped past Lisandro Martinez and burst in behind the defence before squaring neatly for Ngumoha to slam home the third a minute later.

Martinez denied Barcola a fourth with a last-ditch block at the far post while Lammens dived to turn around a powerful Isak strike and clawed a curling Szoboszlai shot around the upright with 15 minutes to go.

Virgil van Dijk headed inches wide from a Wirtz cross, but Victor Munoz swept a sublime fourth eight minutes from time after a lovely reverse pass into the box from Wirtz.

United had the chance of a consolation in stoppage time as sub Joshua Zirkzee broke away and found Fernandes. But the United skipper’s shot was turned wide by Allison.

articles.title: Leny Yoro red card: Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino and Kobbie Mainoo angry at sending off for foul on Liverpool's Alexander Isak
articles.summary: Manchester United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool following Leny Yoro's red card after eight minutes; one of the considerations regarding a red card for Denying of an Obvious Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGS), is the likelihood of the attacking player "keeping or gaining control of the ball"
articles.body:
Pochettino's first United game started in dismal fashion as Yoro was given his marching orders in the eighth minute for bringing down Alexander Isak as the last defender outside the box.

Dominik Szoboszlai then scored from the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz doubled the lead after 13 minutes. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put gloss on the scoreline after half-time.

However, Yoro's sending off was doused in controversy as Isak took a heavy touch into United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before going down under the challenge.

Under the laws, one of the considerations regarding a red card for Denying of an Obvious Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGS), is the likelihood of the attacking player "keeping or gaining control of the ball".

Pochettino felt that not only did Isak lose control of the ball with his touch, but also that United should have been given a penalty for Jeremy Jacquet's challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments before.

"So painful. So disappointed," Pochettino told Sky Sports . "It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

"The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy."

Pushed on whether he was unhappy with Isak's heavy touch, the United boss replied: "The ball was for the goalkeeper.

"In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak. When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

"In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional."

But then Pochettino added: "If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

"How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility, I take the responsibility. We keep pushing."

Pochettino was seen speaking to the officials at full-time and when asked on that, the United boss said: "It's not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important.

"At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card."

United midfielder Mainoo was equally angry at the call. "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card," he said.

"No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is.

"It's 10 vs 11, you come to a place like Anfield, it's a tough game anyway. Then you lose a man, it makes it hard. I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game. We take the pain and move on.

"I wouldn't say it all goes out the window. You can still take the things you did in training into the game, but it makes it 10 times harder with one less man in a situation like that.

"It's hard, it's painful. But no one's coming to save us. We have to work hard, keep digging, keep working, keep fighting. It will all come round."

There was comical defending for the Yoro red-card incident, with United defender Matthijs de Ligt - playing his first Premier League minutes of the season - letting a long ball drop that allowed Isak to run through.

That then led to the Yoro 'foul' - but Roy Keane felt it was unfair on United, even despite their poor defending.

"Isak's not getting the ball," he said. "There's no way he's getting the ball.

"It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble.

"But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again.

"It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not."

Pochettino defended United's defending - as they became the worst defence in Europe when it comes to goals conceded across all competitions this season.

"I wasn't in the past," said Pochettino, referring to United's defensive record under his predecessor Michael Carrick.

"I take responsibility for today, and today we concede four goals with 10 men, and in a circumstance after playing 80 minutes on Anfield with 10 men.

"Of course I take responsibility about that, no worries, but I don't want to compare situations in the past."

Pochettino defends De Ligt selection call

When put to him that United did not have to go and concede four goals after the sending off, he replied: "It's so easy to talk in this way.

"It's about the team, always it's about balance. It's not about one line, the defensive line, the midfield, the offensive. I think when the team concede it is because the balance is not so good, and that I take responsibility about that.

"It's still a lot of games to play. We are in the reality and we need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible and we need to be united, we need to be all together. And I think we feel disappointed because it's clear. It's clear that after eight minutes, it happened what happened, and I think all that the plan was in the bin.

"And what I learn from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games, they want to make the effort, and I think today we made an unbelievable effort.

"I think today was a test. That for me is very positive. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action, Szoboszlai that scored from a free-kick, and 80 minutes to play, more than 80 minutes because I think, you know, the injury time and everything. Do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say? We are in a situation that this is very complicated, it's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort."

One of Pochettino's main decisions was to start De Ligt for the first time in the Premier League in 357 days.

When asked about that, the Argentine said of De Ligt: "He was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty. I think when we arrived, we saw the combination [with Lisandro Martinez].

"And I repeat again, Jacquet was a penalty, and if the referee says that is a penalty, for sure that action after never comes, and maybe we talk in another way.

"But, you know, one centre-back made a mistake, was penalty, wasn't punished, and us, we made one mistake and we were punished. And now I accept all the situation, but the circumstance are the circumstance.

"It's so important to put the circumstance in front. Always."

articles.title: Hull City 2-0 Brighton: Keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis stars for Tigers after Greece nightmare
articles.summary: Nine days after playing for Greece in a nightmare 7-0 loss, keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis plays a pivotal role in Hull's Premier League win against Brighton.
articles.body:
Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic used one word to describe the performance of his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis in Sunday's 2-0 Premier League win against Brighton.

"Unbelievable," he told Match of the Day.

"Especially after the international break, which was very difficult for him."

Tzolakis' previous outing had been for Greece against the Netherlands in the Uefa Nations League, where he and his side were humbled 7-0 by the hosts in Amsterdam.

Nine days later, his contribution to the Tigers' first league victory since 29 August was every bit as important as that of striker Oli McBurnie, who netted both goals in second-half stoppage time against the second-placed Seagulls.

Tzolakis made a series of top saves to keep the highest scorers in the top flight at bay and, when Brighton full-back Costinha was sent off in the 89th minute for a second bookable offence, the hosts seized their opportunity to clinch only their third win following their Premier League return.

McBurnie said the 24-year-old stopper had "kept Hull in a few games" this season and the club were "lucky to have him", while Tzolakis told Sky Sports: "We are a unit and a team.

"We play for each other. We showed a good team effort and we deserved the three points."

McBurnie scores stoppage-time double as Hull stun Brighton

'Always in the right place at the right time'

With the opportunity to move three points behind leaders Arsenal , Brighton looked most likely to score for long spells of Sunday's game, but just could not find a way past former Olympiacos goalkeeper Tzolakis, who joined Hull in August for a reported £20m fee.

He got down to make a vital block early on to deny Diego Gomez, who had slid in to meet a low cross from the left wing. It was the first of several occasions the Paraguay international would be frustrated in front of goal.

Tzolakis then raced out spreadeagled to foil Georginio Rutter with an outstretched left hand - a stop that BBC Radio 5 Live pundit and former striker Clinton Morrison described as "Peter Schmeichel-esque", referring to the legendary Denmark keeper.

Second-half efforts from distance by Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk were dealt with, too.

Yasin Ayari went close with a thumping strike against the bar and when Brighton substitute Charalampos Kostoulas pounced on a short backpass to go through one-on-one, Tzolakis got a hand on his Greece team-mate's shot and Regan Slater was back on the goalline to head the ball to safety.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy, a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said: "We saw again how important Tzolakis is for Hull . He had one of those days where he was always in the right place at the right time.

"When you are a Hull player and you see the kind of saves Tzolakis made when he spread himself and kept it out with his foot, you start thinking that it could be your day.

"It happens a lot in football and, on the flip side, Brighton will have been thinking, 'are we ever going to score here?'."

Hull made a superb start to the campaign after being promoted via the Championship play-offs in May.

They followed victories against Manchester United and Coventry with a draw against Aston Villa - all without conceding a goal.

The Tigers had not won since that 1-0 success at Coventry until beating Brighton - but they are one of four top-flight sides still unbeaten at home and have not lost any fixture by more than a one-goal margin.

They lost 1-0 to champions Arsenal before the international break and Scotland forward McBurnie told Match of the Day: "We know we can make it difficult for the top teams in the league and we've proved that in the past two games.

"We want to make it as difficult as we can for teams to come here and make the MKM Stadium a tough place to come. It's proving that way so far, so long may it continue."

articles.title: TCU fires Sonny Dykes after loss to No. 2 Utah
articles.summary: Dykes led TCU to the national championship game at the end of the 2022 season.
articles.body:
The school announced Sunday that it had fired Dykes, a day after the Horned Frogs lost to No. 2 Utah at home to fall to 5-6. The loss came two weeks after TCU gave up a 28-20 lead late in a 29-28 defeat at Arizona.

"While Sonny's tenure began with the incredible achievement of winning the 2022 Fiesta Bowl and advancing to the national championship game, the proceeding years have seen our program slide further away from that mountain top than can be accepted," TCU athletic director Mike Buddie said in a statement.

TCU defensive coordinator Andy Avalos will be the team's interim coach for Thursday's regular-season finale at Texas Tech. The Horned Frogs need to win that game to be bowl-eligible.

Saturday night, TCU scored 14 points in the third quarter to cut Utah's lead to three and tied the game at 17-17 with just under 10 minutes to go. Utah then ripped off 21 points in the final six minutes of the game for a 38-17 win.

TCU will owe Dykes more than $20 million after he signed a contract extension with the school in April. Before receiving the extension, Dykes' contract was through the 2028 season.

"TCU's investment in football has led to dramatic growth of our university and city in the past 20 years, and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return, especially at such a pivotal time of change in college sports," Buddie said. "We expect to compete for Big 12 championships, to be a central figure in the College Football Playoff conversation, and our continued investment and growth potential reflects that. I expect our new leader will echo those sentiments, rally our fan base behind that challenge, and put a team on the field that our alumni, fans, students, and community will be excited to support."

Dykes was hired at the end of the 2021 season after TCU parted ways with longtime coach Gary Patterson in the middle of the 2021 season. His first season in Fort Worth was storybook until the final game of the season. The Horned Frogs made the College Football Playoff and beat Michigan in the Fiesta Bowl before getting drubbed 65-7 by Georgia in the national championship game.

TCU took a step back in 2023 and went 5-7, but bounced back for 9-4 seasons in both 2024 and 2025. However, the 2026 season got off to a rough start with a loss to Bill Belichick and North Carolina in Week Zero in Ireland. The Horned Frogs have also lost to UCF and West Virginia in 2026 while playing one of the league's toughest schedules. In addition to Utah, Arizona and Texas Tech, TCU also had to play BYU.

As QB Josh Hoover left for Indiana at the end of the 2025 season, the Horned Frogs added former Harvard QB Jaden Craig. However, the offense hasn't been able to get going and Dykes recently fired co-offensive coordinator and offensive line coach A.J. Ricker.

Before coming to TCU, Dykes was the head coach at SMU for five seasons. He went 30-18 with the Mustangs after four seasons at Cal and three at Louisiana Tech. Across 16-plus seasons as a head coach, Dykes has a career record of 112-86.

articles.title: Con Budimir todo es más fácil
articles.standfirst: Osasuna se dispara gracias al solitario gol de su goleador y hunde un poco más al Málaga
articles.summary: Osasuna se dispara gracias al solitario gol de su goleador y hunde un poco más al Málaga
articles.body: Cuando tienes a un delantero como Budimir, la vida es más fácil. El croata volvió a demostrar por qué es ya una leyenda de Osasuna. Un nuevo y solitario gol suyo dio el triunfo a los rojillos para alejarlos del pozo y hundir un poco más a un Málaga que sigue sin saber lo que es ganar en esta Liga. Era un duelo importante para los de Arrasate, que llevaban tres partidos sin ganar (dos derrotas y un empate) desde que ganó en el redebut del técnico vasco y no sacar los tres puntos olía a problemas. En cambio, el triunfo los dispara y acerca ahora a puestos europeos en esta Liga loca que llevamos. Todo lo contrario para el Málaga, que volvió a demostrar que tiene intenciones, pero no pegada. Osasuna lo dejó vivo y no supo aprovecharlo. La permanencia se aleja ahora a siete puntos. Aún hay margen pero las sensaciones siguen siendo malas. Ninguno salió a esperar. Osasuna, por su condición de local. Y el Málaga por sus mayores necesidades. Eso dejó un inicio de partido atractivo en cuanto a ritmo y velocidad de juego, aunque sin ocasiones. Kike Barja tuvo la primera a los 18 minutos tras un centro medido desde la derecha de Rosier, pero su disparo fue bloqueado. Fue la antesala del primer gol rojillo obra, para no perder costumbre, de Budimir, que conectó con un excelente remate de cabeza en plancha otro gran servicio de Rosier tras una buena acción personal en la que se marchó de Larrubia con un giro de 180 grados. El gol terminó por desequilibrar la balanza hacia los de Arrasate, que comenzaron a vivir más en campo rival. Osasuna se imponía desde lo táctico, pero también desde el plano individual, ganando los duelos y finalizando las jugadas que rodaban el área malaguista. De nuevo Barja y Budimir fueron los encargados de ello en una doble ocasión que, entre Herrero y Recio, respectivamente, les negaron. Budimir tuvo otra más apenas un minuto después cuando el reloj ya sobrepasaba la media hora con un remate forzado de volea que se marchó lamiendo el palo. El Málaga necesitaba un cambio de rumbo y Funes lo intentó dando la entrada a Ramón y Puga por Rafa y Pastor tras el descanso. Y a punto estuvo de salirle bien porque al minuto de la reanudación Adrián Niño tuvo en sus botas el empate en un mano a mano que resolvió con una picadita que ser marchó desviada. Osasuna se sacudió rápido el susto con un nuevo remate de Budimir que se estrelló en el larguero. No obstante, sorprendentemente poco más ofreció en la segunda mitad, algo que agradeció un Málaga que se vio vivo en el partido hasta el final. De hecho, Juan Cruz, que entró al campo cerca del ocaso, tuvo la igualada en un remate de cabeza que se fue ligeramente desviado y que contuvo la respiración de todo El Sadar, al igual que un centro envenenado de Puga que pasó por encima de Sergio Herrera.

articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 13 AP Rankings
articles.summary: The Big Ten took a massive hit in the Week 13 AP Top 25.
articles.body:
The Big Ten took a massive hit in the Week 13 AP Top 25.

The UCLA Bruins dropped six positions to No. 10 and the Indiana Hoosiers fell to No. 12 after their losses on Saturday.

UCLA and Indiana's respective tumbles meant that the Big Ten doesn't have a team in the top five of the AP poll since 2021.

However, the Big Ten does have five teams ranked between No. 10 and No. 15. That is significant because all of those programs are in the mix for the final few at-large spots in the 12-team College Football Playoff field.

The Wake Forest Demon Deacons and Texas Tech Red Raiders were the biggest beneficiaries of the UCLA and Indiana losses. They both moved up two spots and into more comfortable positions when it comes to the playoff conversation.

There's also a change in the Group of Six, as the Liberty Flames are now one spot ahead of the Boise State Broncos following Boise State's surprise home loss to the San Diego State Aztecs.

UCLA Falls to No. 10, Indiana Drops to No. 12

The two best teams in the Big Ten going into the final weekend of November are ranked No. 10 and No. 12.

That's a huge shift from previous years when the conference had at least one national championship contender.

UCLA is the more likely playoff participant between it and Indiana because it just suffered its first loss against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday.

However, UCLA has injury concerns at quarterback after backup Ty Dieffenbach was carted off in overtime in Ann Arbor.

Indiana suffered its second defeat of the season on Saturday on the road against the Washington Huskies.

Both teams can still qualify for the postseason, but their margin for error is small.

The Iowa Hawkeyes, Oregon Ducks and USC Trojans are directly behind Indiana in that order.

Oregon has the biggest opportunity in front of it among those teams. The Ducks need to beat the Washington Huskies in Week 13 to confirm their spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. That would open the door for the Ducks to grab the Big Ten's automatic berth into the playoff.

Indiana needs to beat the Purdue Boilermakers and then receive help to qualify for the Big Ten Championship Game. That's a big blow for the reigning champion to get into the playoff field as an at-large.

No. 8 Wake Forest, No. 9 Texas Tech Each Move Up Two Spots

Wake Forest and Texas Tech made important two-spot moves up to Nos. 8 and 9 in Sunday's poll.

Both programs entered Week 12 on the edge of the at-large positions in the playoff picture.

After the losses by UCLA and Indiana, Wake and Texas Tech are in much safer positions. They are two spots ahead of the No. 11 slot, which is the final place for an at-large team in the CFB Playoff rankings.

Wake is already locked into the ACC Championship Game, where it will face the Miami Hurricanes. It needs to get past the Duke Blue Devils first to assure itself of a spot in the top 10 going into December.

Texas Tech has a good probability to make the Big 12 Championship Game to get a shot at the Utah Utes. The Red Raiders just need to handle business against the TCU Horned Frogs on Thanksgiving night to clinch that spot.

The assumption is that Wake Forest and Texas Tech won't be penalized too much for championship game defeats to top-five programs, especially with not many quality candidates beneath them.

No. 21 Liberty Takes Lead in Group of Six Race

The Liberty Flames are the new front-runner to earn the Group of Six's automatic bid to the playoff.

Liberty checked in at No. 21 on Sunday, one spot ahead of Boise State, who lost to San Diego State on Saturday night.

The CFB Playoff selection committee will have its say on Liberty and Boise State on Tuesday, but even if the order flips, the competition is now much closer than it has been all season.

Liberty is 10-1 and already locked into the Conference USA Championship Game, while 9-2 Boise State qualified for the Pac-12 Championship Game.

Both teams need to avoid losses in Week 13 and then attempt to make their best impressions on the committee during conference championship week.

El conjunto dirigido por Pere Romeu tumbó el muro bien defendido por Nanclares con los goles de Camara, Graham, Pajor, Baha y Gurtubay en propia puerta. articles.title: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
articles.summary: United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
articles.body:
If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.

Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola , had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.

The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.

Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.

Was the referee right to send off Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro?

Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.

Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.

VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.

The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.

Was Pochettino right to bench Maguire for Man United?

The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.

For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.

Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.

The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.

The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.

United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.

Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.

A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.

By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.

Their last defeat at Anfield was a 7-0 victory for the home side – a repeat was certainly possible had Liverpool been more clinical.

Matters were so bad that the former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher commented on Sky Sports that he “felt sorry” for de Ligt prior to his eventual substitution in the second half.

The consensus was that Pochettino made the wrong call before the start.

What other Man United changes did Pochettino make at Liverpool?

Yoro and de Ligt have been peripheral figures in their time with the Old Trafford club, for varying reasons including injury, but they were not the only big calls made by Pochettino.

Another injury-plagued player, Patrick Dorgu, was also given a start – and in a formation which was not wholly clear. The popular Amad Diallo was forced to make do with a place on the bench alongside Maguire.

Dorgu, whose form has been indifferent at best, can operate as a wide defender or attacker. It appeared as though he was given some licence on the left to get forward, with United reverting to a back four, Lisandro Martinez covering on the flank in defence and Diogo Dalot holding back on the right.

Whether it was a back four or five to begin with – the latter explaining the absence of the more forward-minded Diallo – United were quickly forced to the latter with the sending-off and the sacrifice of Mbeumo at the other end of the pitch.

Not only was the decision to pick two less experienced centre-backs at Anfield a monumental – and ultimately costly – call, the move to switch to an unfamiliar feel across the backline was a painful lesson for Pochettino, who himself is more accustomed to a 4-2-3-1 setup.

What next for Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino?

With 19th-placed United mired in the Premier League drop zone, the UEFA Champions League appears a sideshow, but a trip to Sporting Lisbon awaits on Wednesday.

In some ways, Europe’s elite club competition, which United have returned to after a three-year absence, may well give Pochettino a free hit to explore how he can get the best out of a beleaguered group.

The absolute priority for the Red Devils has to be channelling their efforts towards climbing the domestic ladder and pulling well away from an unthinkable relegation scrap.

Yoro will be available for the match in the Portuguese capital, which means Pochettino must wrestle with his decision to pick the young duo in defence. Failing to pick both Yoro and de Ligt at Sporting would almost appear an early admission of error.

What is the wider context for Manchester United and Pochettino?

Former United captain Roy Keane was at Anfield as a pundit for Sky Sports and, in his analysis of the overall display, described his old club’s performance at Anfield as “desperate”.

Harsh words for the current playing group are nothing new. Their latest low leaves them with the worst defence record in top-flight football in Europe.

Pochettino at least has time on his side to reverse United’s worst league start in 40 years, but some short-term solutions will be expected by the time Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next Saturday.

Should Pochettino not find some considerable longer-term strategies soon, then the desperate may well turn to the unimaginable.

The heat is turning up for the Red Devils, and the patience of the fans has already run thin with the players this season.

The much-maligned ownership of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos group can also expect prolonged protests, as seen of late.

Change in the dugout appears as though it will not be anywhere near enough to reverse a trend 13 years in the making – and the fans’ unswerving support of Pochettino’s predecessor, Michael Carrick, attests to the fact that wholesale reformation is warranted.

articles.title: Utah’s Devon Dampier stands alone in Big 12 history with another huge performance vs. TCU
articles.summary: The Utah football team remains undefeated on the season, after defeating TCU on Saturday. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier led his squad to a 38-17 victory. D...
articles.body:
The Utah football team remains undefeated on the season, after defeating TCU on Saturday. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier led his squad to a 38-17 victory. Dampier accomplished an incredible feat in the game.

"QB Devon Dampier led the way again, becoming the 1st player in Big 12 history with 3 straight games with 2 pass AND 2 rush TD," ESPN reported on X, formerly Twitter.

Utah is 11-0 on the season. The Utes have had a memorable year under head coach Morgan Scalley, who replaced Kyle Whittingham. Utah is inching closer to a berth in the College Football Playoff.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Utah has the longest active overall and conference winning streaks in FBS, extending its Big 12 run to 13 consecutive victories. The Utes will be back in North Texas in two weeks at the home of the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 4, when they can become the seventh different school in seven years to win the Big 12 title in the conference's last championship game before the College Football Playoff field doubles from 12 to 24," the Associated Press reported.

The Utes had to hold off a pesky TCU team on Saturday. After shutting out TCU in the first half, Utah allowed the Horned Frogs to score 14 points in the third quarter alone.

"Nothing seems to be easy in college football," Utah head coach Morgan Scalley said. "Another game where just back and forth, it seemed like, in terms of momentum. Proud of our guys, the way they finished."

The Utes can finish the regular season at 12-0 if they win their final regular season game. That game is against a struggling West Virginia team on Friday.

Following the loss Saturday, TCU would fire their head coach Sonny Dykes .

articles.title: Augsburg’s Manuel Baum praises rising young African talents Juma Bah and Uchenna Ogundu
articles.summary: FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has praised the contributions of his younger players following Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05. Two of Augsb...
articles.body:
FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has praised the contributions of his younger players following Sunday's 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05. Two of Augsburg's promising young African talents have now scored their first Bundesliga goals on successive matchdays, with Manchester City loanee Juma Bah and Nigerian striker Uchenna Ogundu both making their mark in recent weeks.

Bah, 20, scored Augsburg's second goal against Mainz, while fellow youngster Tim Schnitzer, 18, impressed on his first Bundesliga start. Ogundu, also 20, nearly added a fourth goal after entering as a substitute, striking the inside of the far post in the 81st minute. Asked about Bah's performance at the post-match press conference, Baum took the opportunity to highlight the youthful composition of his team.

"If you look back there, it looked like a child's sweet shop today with Hennes [Behrens, 21], Tim Schnitzer [18], Juma Bah [20]," Baum responded. "Even Yannick Keitel [26] is still young. Marius [Wolf] was the most experienced player."

"The nice thing about seeing players like Juma and others back there is that, despite their age, they're able to gain experience with us," Baum continued. "And one sees what youngsters can achieve when they have a certain level of confidence. Uchi [Uchenna Ugundu, 20] also came in today and hit the post."

Augsburg youngsters celebrate milestone Bundesliga goals

Bah's goal represented an important personal milestone for the Sierra Leone international, who returned from suspension to help Baum contend with the absences of Jeffrey Gouweleeuw, Chrislain Matsima, Noahkai Banks, and Calvin Brackelmann.

As Get German Football News reported when Bah completed his loan move from Manchester City in September, Augsburg secured a purchase option reportedly worth €21.5m for the young defender. Bah arrived with considerable senior experience from previous spells at Lens and Nice, but has faced competition for playing time in the Bavarian Swabian defence.

Sunday's performance offered another indication of what the club hopes to gain from the arrangement. Bah bundled home following Fabian Rieder's 36th-minute corner to double Augsburg's advantage and helped the makeshift back-three protect the lead.

Ogundu's first Bundesliga goal came a fortnight earlier, with the Nigerian polishing off a Fabian Rieder through ball in second-half injury time of Augsburg's 5-2 defeat to RB Leipzig. Speaking in an interview published in Augsburg's matchday programme ahead of Sunday's Mainz encounter , Ogundu described the goal as a proud personal moment, albeit one tempered by the disappointing result.

The 20-year-old identified his speed as his greatest asset and expressed satisfaction with his technical and tactical development since arriving in the Bundesliga. Ogundu also spoke of the support he has received from his teammates, singling out Keitel, Michael Gregoritsch, and Behrens as particularly helpful in making him feel at home in the Fuggerstadt.

The Nigerian, whom GGFN covered extensively following his expensive winter transfer from Alanyaspor , arrived in Augsburg amid stiff competition for places in attack. Our 2026/27 Augsburg tactical preview identified Ogundu as one of the winners of preseason preparations, while cautioning that his opportunities would remain limited by the presence of more established attacking options.

His first Bundesliga goal and lively substitute appearance against Mainz nevertheless suggest that Ogundu is beginning to make a stronger case for playing time. Baum's comments suggest that the FCA trainer remains encouraged by the progress of his younger players. With Schnitzer also delivering an impressive starting XI debut, Sunday's victory provided Augsburg with more than just a welcome three points.

The injury crisis may have forced Baum's hand, but the performances of his emerging talents have offered him several additional options moving forward.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena

articles.title: I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool as he endured the worst debut by a Manchester United manager in 100 years. N...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool as he endured the worst debut by a Manchester United manager in 100 years.

Not since player-manager Lal Hilditch lost 4-0 to Bolton in October 1926 had a new boss endured such a chastening start, which left the club 19th in the Premier League, two points away from climbing out of the bottom three.

But while the head coach said he took full ownership of the result, he felt the eighth-minute red card shown to Leny Yoro changed the course of the game.

The defender's dismissal for denying Alexander Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake allowed Dominik Szoboszlai to score from the resulting free-kick.

A brilliant twisting volley from Florian Wirtz, his fifth goal in four games for club and country, doubled the lead and while Liverpool should have added plenty more, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz compounded a chastening evening for Pochettino in the second half.

It proved too much for some fans in the visiting section with police called to deal with a disturbance with one man being led away in handcuffs.

"It is painful because it is 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men. I take responsibility for that, no worries," said Pochettino, who argued a challenge by Jeremy Jacquet on Bryan Mbeumo before the red card should have resulted in a penalty.

"We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is true.

"You need to look at the circumstance because it is so easy to talk so cheap. We lose one game; we are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today.

"We have a lot of work to do and we take responsibility. We feel the pain but the thing is to keep working."

United have conceded 23 goals in 11 league matches and Pochettino's decision to hand De Ligt his first Premier League start in a year drew scrutiny, which only increased with the defender's performance.

"The team concede because the balance is not so good and I take responsibility for that," said the Argentinian.

"He (De Ligt) was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived we saw the combinations."

Asked whether he had inherited a relegation battle, Pochettino added: "Still a lot of games to play. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together.

"We feel disappointed because it is clear after what happened (Yoro's red card) happened the plan was in the bin.

"What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games.

"Today we made an effort. Today was a test that, for me, is very positive."

Victory was only Liverpool's second at home in the league this season and head coach Andoni Iraola celebrated with Jurgen Klopp-style fist pumps as his side moved into fourth.

"Always I enjoy the moment. I think we owe them (the fans) because we have had much better results away and we want to solve this and want to give them a big win and more to celebrate," he said.

The game was Wirtz's best for the club as in addition to his goal he created 10 chances, providing the assist for Munoz's goal.

"I think he has been playing very well for a long, sustained period of time, he finished before the break with a goal and assist against Palace," said the Liverpool boss.

"He has been playing well for a while but still he is giving us a lot."

articles.title: UCLA falls to No. 10 in the US LBM Coaches Poll after loss to Michigan
articles.summary: UCLA fell from No. 4 to No. 10 in the USA TODAY US LBM Coaches Poll after the 18-16 triple-overtime loss to the Michigan Wolverines.
articles.body:
It comes as no surprise that the UCLA Bruins dropped in this week's USA TODAY US LBM Coaches Poll following the team's first loss of the season. UCLA fell from No. 4 to No. 10 after the 18-16 triple-overtime loss to the Michigan Wolverines .

It was a rough Saturday for the Big Ten teams, with Indiana and Ohio State falling significantly after losses in Week 12. UCLA's drop of six spots was tied for the largest fall in this week's poll. Kentucky and Indiana each dropped seven spots, with the Bruins and Boise State falling six spots.

The slate only gets tougher for UCLA, facing No. 15 USC but will very likely be without quarterback Ty Dieffenbach . Dieffenbach was injured in overtime of Saturday's loss, with Madden Iamaleava coming in to replace him.

Georgia remains at the No. 1 spot, followed by Utah, Notre Dame, Miami (FL) and Alabama. UCLA is still the highest-ranked Big Ten Conference team at No. 10 ahead of No. 12 Indiana, No. 13 Iowa, No. 14 Oregon, No. 15 USC. Nebraska, Ohio State, Washington, Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota all receiving votes in this week's poll.

UCLA is in need of a win in Week 13 against the Trojans . A win would secure a spot in the Big Ten Conference title game and could very well get the Bruins into the College Football Playoff. Without Dieffenbach, it'll be very tough to have enough offense to defeat the Trojans, which would only drop UCLA farther down in the polls.
